title: Founding Finance Lead
description:
**Why This Role**

* Be the Lead Finance Person – You're the first dedicated finance hire at a startup with significant, accelerating revenue, building the financial rigor behind the growth rather than reporting into a finance org of 50.
* Work with the General Manager – Build the models behind every major decision the company makes: pricing, market entry, hiring, capital allocation, and the story we tell future investors.
* Own the Numbers – Stop evaluating other people's companies from the diligence side and apply your reps inside one fast-growing business, where your analysis becomes the decision.
* Ground Floor Opportunity – Join an early-stage startup led by a repeat founder with a successful exit.

**What You'll Do**

* Build and own Concourse's operating model: revenue forecasting, unit economics, headcount planning, and scenario analysis across the business
* Partner with the CEO on strategic decisions (new market entry, pricing, capital allocation, and partnership economics) by building the models that frame the options clearly
* Develop and maintain KPIs and financial reporting that give leadership a real-time view of the business: what's working, what's at risk, and where to push harder
* Lead ad-hoc analyses as the business demands: competitive benchmarking, build vs. buy analysis, contract economics, and investor-facing materials
* Drive fundraise preparation and investor communications, bringing a banker's polish to the data room, the model, and the narrative
* Build the financial infrastructure from scratch: the processes, templates, and reporting cadence that will scale with the company
* Serve as the internal finance partner to company leadership, helping them understand what the numbers mean and how to use them
* Use AI tools to scale your work: automating reporting, accelerating analysis, and building leverage a traditional finance team gets from headcount

**What We're Looking For**

* 3-4 years of combined investment banking and private equity experience
* Elite financial modeling and forecasting skills; you can build a three-statement model, bottoms-up revenue forecast, or KPI dashboard from a blank spreadsheet
* Sharp instincts for the story behind the numbers. You don't just report metrics, you interpret them and recommend action
* AI-pilled: you already use tools like Claude to 10x your output, you reach for AI before you reach for an analyst, and you want to build a finance function that's AI-native from day one
* Ability to operate independently in an unstructured environment; there's no playbook here, and you'll need to write it
* Clear, direct communicator, comfortable presenting analysis to a founder/CEO and pushing back when the assumptions don't hold
* Based in NYC + work in-person in Flatiron (5 days/week)

**About Concourse**
Concourse is the fastest-growing govtech, providing software to more than 100 state and local governments across the U.S.
  
  
Government calls what we do "IT modernization." We call it a trillion-dollar opportunity to overhaul how government works. Public services are broken not because of bureaucracy but instead because they run on antiquated, user-unfriendly software from legacy vendors.
  
  
Some examples: Concourse is powering the legislative management system for one of America's largest cities, a state's entire online bail payment system, and a case-management platform for mental-health response teams.
  
  
We are an AI-native company. Our org structure and staffing model are radically different from those of legacy tech companies: we have a flat team of superstar generalists who both own client relationships and manage fleets of long-horizon AI agents.
  
  
Our team works together in our Flatiron office five days a week.
  
  
Compensation Range: $150K - $200K

description:
**Head of Finance**
===================

**About the Role**
------------------

We're looking for a Head of Finance to build Shade's finance function as we rapidly scale. You'll own planning, modeling, reporting, and the financial systems behind them, and you'll be the person leadership turns to when a decision depends on the numbers. Today, our finances run on QuickBooks and spreadsheets that worked for an early-stage company. Your job is to turn that into a finance engine that keeps pace with our growth. This is a hands-on seat. You'll build the models yourself, set up the reporting cadence, and help with our next financing. You'll work directly with our CEO as his partner on everything finance. We expect this role to be in-office 4 days a week - we have a cool office in NYC!

**Our Mission**
---------------

Shade is scaling fast. In a year and a half, we've built the combined capabilities of Frame.io (acquired by Adobe for $1.275B) and LucidLink ($40M ARR) and paired them with proprietary AI search and labeling. We handle thousands of hours of video and tens of millions of requests every day, and we're critical infrastructure for post-production houses, creative agencies, sports teams, and in-house media teams at large companies. Customers include Meta, The New York Times, Grüns, HelloFresh, and Clay. We're growing 150% QoQ with 120% NRR.

Backed by Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, Contrary, SignalFire, and Bling.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Own the operating model, annual budget, and rolling forecast
* Build scenario models for hiring plans, pricing, new market bets, and fundraising outcomes
* Run monthly close, budget-vs-actuals, and board and investor reporting
* Track and report core SaaS metrics: ARR, NRR, burn multiple, CAC payback, gross margin, and runway
* Know what “good” looks like and can describe it - seen a growing business with good metrics, and operational changes relative to financial guidance.
* Partner with Sales and RevOps on quotas, commissions, and deal desk; partner with Ops on payroll and spend controls
* Set up the controls, policies, and processes a company of our size needs, without slowing the team down
* Bring a financial lens to every major decision, push back when the numbers don't support a plan, and take real ownership of finance

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

* 6-8 years of experience in finance, including building finance systems at a Series B+ startup. You know what finance looks like when there’s no playbook and the company changes every quarter.
* Ideally, you started your career in venture capital, investment banking, or consulting, and you know how investors read a company.
* You're excellent in Excel (or Google Sheets), and you use AI tools like Claude to work faster. You build three-statement models, scenario analyses, and forecasts from scratch, and they hold up under scrutiny.
* Ideally, you have a background in accounting. You’ve worked hands-on with an ERP or accounting system, QuickBooks included.
* You understand SaaS metrics and can connect them to cash, runway, and valuation.
* You're comfortable owning both the strategic work (fundraising, planning) and the details (close, reconciliations, vendor terms).
* You communicate clearly with non-finance people and can turn a model into a one-page recommendation.
* Low ego, high ownership, and comfortable building process where it doesn't exist yet.
* You operate at a fast pace, can clearly articulate how you work, and are energized by sparring with a hands-on founder.

**How We Work**
---------------

Our team is flexible, moves quickly, and is always looking at new technologies and ideas that can speed up our work and improve our processes. We value people who take ownership, communicate proactively, and bring fresh ideas. You won't be handed a finished playbook. You'll write it.

**How We Hire**
---------------

We skip the standard pitch and 30-60-90 presentation. Our onsite is a working session: we'll share real context about where we are and work through live challenges together, and you'll meet the team. It's the closest thing to doing the job, and it lets you evaluate us as much as we evaluate you.

**Compensation**
----------------

* $200,000-$250,000 base salary
* Meaningful equity participation
* Medical, dental & vision insurance
* 401k with % match
* Unlimited PTO
* Gym membership @ Lifetime

*At Chanel, we are focused on creating an inclusive culture that nurtures personal growth, contributing to collective progress. We believe the uniqueness of each individual increases the diversity, complementarity and effectiveness of our teams. We strongly encourage your application, as we value the perspective, experience and potential you could bring to CHANEL.*

**About the Role:**

CHANEL is seeking a Senior Group Director, Boutique Excellence, Northeast Region to lead the regional execution of Boutique Excellence priorities across Retail Operations, Performance, and Transformation.

  

Reporting to the Head of Boutique Excellence, USA, with a dotted-line relationship to the Head of Retail, Northeast, this leader will serve as the key connection between corporate Boutique Excellence teams and the regional retail organization. The role will ensure that operational standards, performance priorities, and transformation initiatives are translated into clear, practical, and consistent execution across Fashion Boutiques, lease doors, and Multi-Brand Select locations.

  

This leader will partner closely with regional retail leadership to strengthen operational excellence, enable data-informed decisions, support planning cycles, and ensure new initiatives are effectively embedded in the field.

  

**What Impact You Can Create at CHANEL:**

Regional Boutique Excellence Leadership

* Serve as the regional leader and primary liaison for Boutique Excellence, aligning corporate priorities with the needs of the Northeast retail organization.
* Partner with the Head of Retail, Senior Group Directors of Retail, and boutique leaders within the Northeast region to establish clear priorities, drive accountability, and enable consistent execution.
* Foster a connected regional community across Boutique, lease, and Multi-Brand Select locations, sharing best practices and strengthening consistency in ways of working.
* Translate regional feedback, business needs, and opportunities into actionable insights for the corporate Boutique Excellence team.
  

  

Retail Operations

* Bachelor’s degree required.

title: Recruiter, Life Sciences & Medtech
description:
**Panther: Better Health Is Skin Deep**
=======================================

Panther is unlocking the tremendous biological power of our skin, delivering efficacious, shelf-stable treatments directly to customers. Panther's precisely engineered smart microarray patches (SmartPatches) address a wide range of needs in Skin Health (cosmetics, medical aesthetics) and are designed to treat conditions in Systemic Health (infectious diseases, allergies, cancer, autoimmune diseases, metabolic disorders). Billions of people around the world lack access to effective treatment, and we will change this.

SmartPatches enable effective, tech-enabled customer experiences, and our AI platform provides valuable insights for improved patient outcomes and the development of even better treatments. SmartPatches are affordable to manufacture and distribute, and easy to apply, resulting in greater access and market expansion. Panther is developing clinically validated products, the first of which launches in 2027.

**The Opportunity**
===================

Panther is about to launch Pique Labs, our first skincare brand, and we're looking for a full-cycle life sciences and medtech recruiter to own hiring through our biggest growth stretch yet. Many of our departments are already built, and over the next six months they will grow significantly across R&D, engineering, manufacturing, quality and commercial roles, from co-ops and engineers to senior leaders. You will run recruiting for Panther end to end.

You will own every step: kicking off searches with hiring managers, writing job descriptions, sourcing and screening candidates, running the interview process, closing offers together with hiring managers, and welcoming new hires on day one. You will partner directly with our leadership team and scientific and engineering leaders in New York and Pittsburgh, and every hire you make will shape how Panther builds its first products. You won't be starting from scratch.

Our processes are already in place so you can hit the ground running, and you'll be supported by our Ashby ATS, an AI agent trained on Panther's culture, team and processes that helps evaluate candidates, and other tools. Panther will keep adding recruiting tools and support through 2027.

**The role starts as a contract, with a real path to a full-time role as Panther grows. Remote contractors must be available during Eastern Time business hours, and full-time roles require relocating to New York City.**

**The Impact You'll Make here**
===============================

* Help Panther hit its goals on time by staffing every team with great people who share our values and bring the skills and experience each team needs.
* Panther's priority scientific, engineering, manufacturing and commercial roles are filled with strong hires, on time, across New York and Pittsburgh.
* Every open role has a kickoff, a clear job description, a clear strategy and a defined interview process.
* Hiring managers and the CEO get a clear weekly view of every search, and Ashby is accurate and up to date.
* Candidates have a fast, respectful experience, and offers close at the right level within our ranges.
* New hires arrive ready for day one, with onboarding coordinated with their manager and team.

**What You Will Do**
====================

***Build and Source Every Search***
-----------------------------------

* Own multiple open roles at once across R&D, formulation, process and device engineering, manufacturing, quality, regulatory and commercial, from co-ops and technical individual contributors to senior leaders and executives.
* Run kickoffs with hiring managers to define the role, must-haves, interview panel and timeline, then write and post the job description.
* Map target companies and talent for each search, across medical device, biotech, pharma, CDMOs and CMOs, dermatology and skincare brands, and complex manufacturing.
* Source passive candidates through LinkedIn and creative channels beyond it, such as referrals, conferences and trade shows, patents and scientific publications, professional associations, alumni networks, investor and advisor networks, and university programs like the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon.
* Use AI-powered sourcing and outreach tools alongside LinkedIn to find hard-to-reach talent, and build pipelines ahead of upcoming roles so searches start warm.

***Lead, Screen, Interview and Decide***
----------------------------------------

* Review inbound applications in Ashby using our evaluation framework and AI-assisted screening.
* Run recruiter screens that test both technical fit and culture fit, and share a short assessment after each, with strengths, concerns and a clear recommendation: Move forward, Hold or Reject.
* Design each role's interview process, including who tests what and when to use a take-home assignment or technical presentation.
* Coordinate scheduling, from CEO interviews to in-person final rounds in New York and Pittsburgh, and lead debriefs so decisions happen fast.
* Keep candidate trackers and shortlists scored against each role's criteria, and give every candidate a respectful experience.

***Close, Onboard and Run Recruiting***
---------------------------------------

* Benchmark compensation for life sciences and medtech roles, recommend offers within our ranges, explain early-stage stock options, and close offers with hiring managers.
* Run reference checks, prepare offer letters, and coordinate welcome emails and first-day logistics.
* Report weekly to the CEO and leadership on pipeline, progress and risks.
* Support headcount planning and help prioritize roles against the hiring plan.
* Keep our careers site and postings up to date, and manage recruiting tools and spend, such as LinkedIn Recruiter and job ads.
* Use AI every day to work faster, from sourcing to writing job descriptions and candidate summaries.

**Role Summary**
================

*At Pfizer, breakthroughs change patients' lives. In Specialty Care that means people living with rare and serious conditions, from ATTR amyloidosis and hemophilia to atopic dermatitis and vitiligo. Our Integrated Insights & Strategy (IIS) team turns data into the decisions that help these medicines reach the patients who need them, powered by a proprietary, AI-enabled analytics stack few commercial teams can match. As a Team Lead in IIS, you will build and lead the team of strategists behind how these brands grow, and grow the people who do it.*

Pfizer's Specialty Care Integrated Insights & Strategy (IIS) team is seeking a Director / Team Lead who will build, lead, and develop a brand-aligned pod of strategists and analysts. The team drives commercial brand strategy by framing the business problems, generating the insights and analytics that answer them, and enabling executional excellence.

The Team Lead is a trusted thought partner to senior US and Global portfolio and TA leaders, sitting on their leadership teams and bringing analyses that shape portfolio decisions and overarching strategy. Just as importantly, they grow the people: unlocking the team's intellectual and analytical curiosity, fostering a spirit of innovation and out-of-the-box thinking, setting a high bar for quality, and mentoring the next generation of IIS strategists.

The ideal candidate is an outstanding people leader with the EQ to build and inspire cross-functional teams and guide the delivery of exceptional strategic consultancy. They bring proven thought leadership in their space, strong entrepreneurial drive, and a well-formed point of view they are not afraid to assert, and they develop that same confidence in their team through consistent mentorship and support. They pair deep analytic command with the presence to partner credibly with senior leaders, and they measure their success by the decisions they shape and the people they grow.

**Why IIS: What You'll Gain**
=============================

* Lead at the frontier of AI in commercial analytics. Your team uses and helps shape IIS-built tools like ORBIT (our subnational performance platform) and AnalogueOS (our AI analogue-matching engine), and you will set how AI fluency scales across the pod.
* A leadership platform. You will build and grow a team of high-caliber strategists and analysts, shape how the pod works in an AI-enabled operating model, and see your people advance along IIS's strategist career track.
* A real seat at the table. You will sit on senior portfolio and TA leadership teams as a trusted thought partner, and your team's analysis shapes the decisions those leaders make.
* A culture built on curiosity. We reward the sharper question, out-of-the-box thinking, and genuine intellectual partnership over order-taking, and we look to our leaders to protect it.

**Role Responsibilities**
=========================

**Team Leadership & Development**
---------------------------------

* Build, lead, and develop a brand-aligned pod of strategists and analysts, hiring for judgment and curiosity and growing each person's craft and career.
* Mentor and coach the team to frame sharper questions, form and assert a point of view, and deliver exceptional strategic consultancy.
* Foster a culture of innovation, intellectual curiosity, and high-quality work, setting the standard and removing barriers so the team can do its best thinking.
* Shape how the pod operates in an AI-enabled model, building the capability, fluency, and ways of working that scale.

**Portfolio & Brand Strategy Partnership**
------------------------------------------

* Serve as a trusted thought partner to senior US and Global portfolio and TA leaders, sitting on their leadership teams to inform investment decisions with rigorous analysis.
* Direct the team to frame, investigate, and answer the key business questions behind commercial strategy and tactics, and to connect research and analytics into a clear, persuasive story with actionable recommendations for senior leadership.
* Oversee development of the in-house knowledge base that drives patient and HCP insight.

**Performance, Forecasting & Operating-Plan Oversight**
-------------------------------------------------------

* Oversee the team's brand and portfolio performance measurement and reporting, and its contribution to QBRs, using IIS models and dashboards.
* Oversee development of Long-Range Forecasts (LRFs) and Operating Plans in partnership with US, Global, and Forecasting CoE colleagues, including epi- and trend-based models.
* Ensure accurate, timely performance measurement and a clear articulation of what the data means for the business.

**Cross-Functional Leadership & Capability**
--------------------------------------------

* Lead the integration of insights across cross-functional analytics teams (data science, analytics engineering, market research, and media), and advance the use of novel data sources including real-world data.
* Advance team capabilities through thought leadership and knowledge sharing, and keep activities aligned and cohesive with stakeholders.

title: Associate Director, Proposition Strategy
description:
Spotify's Propositions team is responsible for what we offer and how we package it — the plans, tiers, and offerings that determine how hundreds of millions of people experience and pay for Spotify. As Associate Director, Proposition Strategy, you'll help shape Spotify's proposition portfolio: evaluating new opportunities, shaping packaging structures, and building the commercial case for where we invest.
  
  
This is a globally focused role for someone who thinks in business cases as much as in ideas. You'll be a commercial engine for the team, assessing the financial upside, risks, and trade-offs of each opportunity and bringing clear prioritization recommendations to senior leadership. The role is centered on strategic evaluation and decision-making rather than downstream execution or launch. You'll have broad exposure across multiple strategic priorities and work closely with partners across the business to anticipate where propositions should go next.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Evaluate the commercial and economic viability of new propositions — including new offerings, complementary products, and packaging structures.
* Build robust business cases end to end, from initial hypothesis through sizing, unit economics, and scenario modelling to an executive-ready recommendation.
* Partner closely with Finance and Licensing to validate assumptions, pressure-test models, and quantify the financial impact and licensing implications of different propositions.
* Assess upside, risk, and trade-offs across the portfolio to drive clear prioritization decisions on which opportunities to pursue.
* Develop a portfolio strategy that balances near- and long-term opportunities and creates more value for Spotify's listeners and business.
* Build strong relationships across Product and other functions to understand the innovation roadmap and proactively identify commercialization opportunities.
* Track the competitive and macro landscape to anticipate how proposition and packaging strategy should evolve over time.

Who You Are
  
  

* 8+ years of experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, product or monetization strategy, business development, or a similar commercial role — with a track record of turning ambiguous problems into structured, executive-ready recommendations.
* Expert in building and owning complex financial models and business cases: unit economics, revenue and pricing analysis, scenario modelling, and cannibalization frameworks.
* Experienced in subscription, consumer, or digital media businesses, ideally with exposure to pricing, packaging, or bundling across global markets.
* A sound commercial decision-maker who can weigh competing opportunities, make clear prioritization calls, and defend them with data.
* A strong communicator and trusted partner who can distill complex commercial trade-offs into crisp narratives for senior leadership and influence without authority.
* Comfortable operating with breadth — equally at home in a spreadsheet, a cross-functional working session, and a leadership review.
* Curious and forward-looking, with a strong point of view on how product innovation can translate into new ways to create and capture customer value.

Where You'll Be
  
  

* This role is based in New York
* We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The United States base range for this position is $191,274–$273,249, plus equity. These ranges may be modified in the future.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. Find our AI notice here: https://lifeatspotify.com/ai-notice

Courier Health is on a mission to solve one of the biggest and most meaningful opportunities in healthcare: reinvent how people living with chronic and rare diseases are supported.
  
  
We are building the future of patient engagement for life sciences companies. Our software is leveraged by biopharma companies to support patients in their complex journey from diagnosis to initiating and remaining on therapy to achieve optimal health outcomes.
  
  
Come Build with Us
  
  
We’re a NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We’re an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. If that sounds like your kind of place, we think you’ll love it here.
  
  
The Opportunity
  
  
Courier Health is signing faster than the function around our sales team can currently support. We exist to get patients faster, better access to life-saving therapies, and every program we win is another population we reach. What determines how fast that happens is no longer just how well we sell. I’s how we price, where we point the team, how the hard deals get structured, and whether leadership can see what’s actually working. This role owns that.
  
  
As Head of Sales Strategy & Operations, you’ll report to the Chief Commercial Officer and own everything that sits around the sales organization: pricing and packaging, deal desk, territory and coverage, commercial analytics, planning cadence, enablement, and the systems underneath all of it. You’ll also be the connection point between Sales and Product, Product Marketing, and Finance.
  
  
Most of this is still being written. The pricing frameworks, the approval model, the metrics leadership runs the business on, you’ll build them and then run them. If you’ve spent your career tuning someone else’s commercial engine, this is the seat where you design it. The calls you make in your first year become how Courier Health goes to market for the next five.
  
  
What You’ll Build
  
  
**Pricing, packaging, and how deals get done.**
You’ll own what we charge, what’s bundled, and what a new capability is worth to a customer and keep evolving it as the product moves. Underneath that, you’ll build the deal desk: structure, terms, approvals, and real partnership with sellers on the opportunities that matter most. Done right, the framework makes deals move faster, not slower.
  
  
**A coverage model that scales ahead of the pipeline.**
Segmentation, territory design, account prioritization, and the capacity math that tells us when to hire and where to aim. You’ll work with the CCO and executive team on where we play (which segments, which use cases, which commercial models) and turn those calls into plans the sales team can actually run. Then you’ll set the operating rhythm that keeps it honest: pipeline reviews, forecasting, target setting, business reviews.
  
  
**A commercial picture leadership can act on.**
Pipeline health, conversion, cycle length, win/loss, segment performance, productivity - defined once, measured consistently, and reported in a form that changes decisions instead of describing them. You’ll own the systems and data underneath it too: CRM strategy, sales workflows, data standards, and the tooling that gives sellers their time back. You’ll partner with Finance on the forecast and own the read on why the numbers look the way they do.
  
  
**A sales team that gets better every quarter.**
Onboarding, playbooks, methodology, and competitive resources built so sellers understand the customer’s problem, not just our product. You’ll also be the channel back: deal patterns, loss reasons, unmet needs, and market intelligence reaching Product and Product Marketing on a schedule rather than by accident. ICPs, positioning, and launch readiness should reflect what’s actually happening in live deals.
  
  
What Makes You Successful
  
  

* 10+ years in sales strategy, revenue operations, commercial strategy, or management consulting, including 3+ years leading the function at a high-growth B2B software company.
* Hands-on depth in pricing and packaging, deal structuring, territory design, and commercial analytics. You’ve built these, not inherited them.
* Exceptional analytical ability. You can get to the insight yourself and make it legible to an executive audience in one page.
* A track record of building process a team actually adopted and kept without adding drag to the sale.
* Strong command of enterprise sales dynamics: long cycles, multiple stakeholders, real procurement.
* Credibility with executives, including the willingness to disagree with one when the data says to.
* Comfortable moving between the framework and the spreadsheet. You’d rather build the model than wait for one.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, especially turning commercial data into a recommendation someone can act on.
* Comfortable with autonomy and ambiguity at an early-stage company.

**Bonus Points If You Have**

* Experience in life sciences, healthcare, or health tech.
* Built a deal desk from scratch.
* Worked closely with Product and Product Marketing on positioning, launches, and competitive intelligence.

title: Manager, Business Insights
description:
We are seeking a highly analytical Business Insights Manager with experience in the book publishing industry to support financial planning, sales forecasting, and strategic decision-making. This role will leverage predictive modeling, historical sales data, market trends, consumer behavior insights, and publishing-specific performance drivers to develop accurate sales and financial projections.
  
  
The ideal candidate combines strong FP&A and forecasting capabilities with expertise in data analytics and predictive modeling. This position will partner closely with Finance, Sales, Marketing, Publishing, Inventory Planning, and Executive Leadership to provide actionable insights that optimize revenue growth, inventory management, and profitability.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Forecasting & Predictive Analytics**

* Develop and maintain predictive models to forecast book sales across frontlist and backlist titles, formats, channels, imprints, and territories.
* Analyze historical sales trends, seasonality, title performance, author performance, promotional activity, metadata, and market dynamics to improve forecast accuracy.
* Build statistical and machine learning models to project sales, revenue, gross margin, inventory requirements, returns, and royalty obligations.
* Create scenario analyses and sensitivity models to evaluate key assumptions, launch strategies, pricing changes, and market shifts.
* Monitor forecast performance using defined accuracy metrics and continuously refine methodologies based on actual results.

**Financial Planning & Analysis**

* Analyze revenue, gross margin, inventory, working capital, and title-level profitability.
* Support executive management with ad hoc financial modeling, investment analysis, and strategic decision support.
* Contribute to executive and board-level reporting and presentations.

**Publishing Industry Analysis**

* Evaluate title-level performance and profitability across authors, imprints, categories, formats, retailers, and distribution channels.
* Support print-run, reprint, inventory, and demand-planning decisions through forecast-driven recommendations.
* Monitor industry trends, competitive activity, consumer buying patterns, and retailer dynamics.
* Provide forecasting support for licensing, subsidiary rights, special sales, digital publishing, and client-publisher arrangements.
* Partner with Sales, Editorial, Marketing, Production, and Operations to incorporate commercial assumptions into forecasts.

**Data, Reporting & Controls**

* Design and maintain dashboards, KPI reporting, and automated forecast routines.
* Extract, transform, validate, and analyze large datasets from ERP, royalty, sales, inventory, and business intelligence systems.
* Maintain clear model documentation, assumptions, version control, and reconciliation processes to support auditability and management review.
* Present complex analyses in a concise, business-focused manner to finance leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

**Qualifications Education & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, or a related field; MBA, CFA, or advanced analytics certification is a plus.
* 3-7 years of experience in FP&A, financial analysis, sales forecasting, demand planning, or a related analytical role.
* Experience in book publishing is strongly preferred; experience in media, content, licensing, or another intellectual property-driven business may also be relevant.
* Demonstrated experience building revenue forecasts and predictive models using large, complex datasets.
* Experience with title profitability, inventory, returns, royalties, or publishing sales channels is highly desirable.

**Technical Skills**

* Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including Power Query, Power Pivot, advanced formulas, and financial modeling.
* Proficiency in SQL and experience with Python or R for predictive analytics and statistical modeling.
* Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or a comparable visualization platform.
* Knowledge of forecasting methods such as time-series modeling, regression analysis, seasonal trend analysis, and machine learning techniques.
* Experience with ERP and reporting platforms such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, or publishing-specific systems.

**Core Competencies**

* Strong analytical judgment and problem-solving skills
* Ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable business insights
* Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to data integrity
* Effective written, verbal, and presentation skills
* Strategic thinking, commercial awareness, and strong business partnering
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

**Success Measures**

* Improved forecast accuracy for title-level and consolidated sales projections
* Reduced inventory obsolescence, stock-outs, and excess working capital through improved demand forecasting
* More informed acquisition, print-run, pricing, promotion, and inventory decisions
* Scalable, well-documented forecasting and reporting processes

**Compensation & Work Arrangement**
Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits, with bonus eligibility and hybrid work flexibility, as applicable. Final compensation and work arrangement will be based on company policy, experience, and location.

title: Manager, Brand Planning, GS
description:
**About Gap**
-------------

Gap has always been about optimistic American style. Starting with our very first store on Ocean Avenue in San Francisco, opened almost 50 years ago by Doris and Don Fisher. The thread that’s run through those five decades is the phenomenal people that make up our brand – our employees and our customers. People who are rooted in the legacy that makes Gap what it is, but who are also focused on the future. People who want to leave the world better than they found it.

We’ve built our brand on staying true to our roots while always being out in front of what’s next. If you want to be part of an iconic American brand, and help lead the way for where we’re headed, we’d love to have you join us.

**About the role**
------------------

The Brand Planning lead is an essential contributor to the end-to-end management of the Gap/Gap Outlet business, sitting at the intersection of investment strategy, product strategy, and customer experience. Through close cross-functional partnership across the inventory management, merchandising, site merchandising, company planning, and commercial planning organizations, the brand planning lead facilitates all key business processes, and works as a close counterpart to the brand IM lead to foster data-based decision-making in weekly business management, monthly open-to-buy forecasting, and at key inventory investment milestones. This role provides significant exposure to leadership across the Gap/Gap Outlet organization, and helps provide, brand-wide perspective, and recommendations on business performance, risks, and opportunities.

**What you'll do**
------------------

**In-Season**

* Review business results in partnership with brand IM lead and divisional merchandise planning teams, and identifying actions to optimize KPIs
* Partner with merchandise planning, commercial planning, and pricing to validate commercial plan strategy, hindsight promotions, and guide future strategy
* Guide the merchandise planning team through the monthly open-to-buy process: provide timelines and forecasting guidance to the merchandise planning team; review forecast roll and identify risks + opportunities vs the finance forecast/budget; publish monthly receipt reconciliation data
* Work with company planning partners to hand off key forecast inputs (receipts, markdown conversion) and understand any variances between tops down/bottoms up forecasts
* Partner with brand inventory management lead to prepare for monthly forecast discussions with brand leadership
* Analyze business results and trend outlooks to identify emerging risks and opportunities, and recommend actions needed to achieve financial and operational targets.

**Title:** **Director of Finance**  
**Report to:** **Executive Director**  
**Status:** **Full Time Exempt**  
  
El Museo del Barrio, founded by a coalition of Puerto Rican educators, artists, and activists, is the nation’s leading Latino and Latin American cultural institution. The Museum welcomes visitors of all backgrounds to discover the artistic landscape of these communities through its extensive Permanent Collection, varied exhibitions and publications, bilingual public programs, educational activities, festivals, and special events.  
  
**SCOPE AND PURPOSE OF ROLE**  
  
The Director of Finance is responsible for safeguarding El Museo del Barrio’s financial health and long-term sustainability through proactive financial management, disciplined budgeting, effective cash flow oversight, and accurate financial reporting. Working closely with the Executive Director and Board of Trustees, the Director provides the financial leadership, analysis, and recommendations necessary to maintain a strong and stable financial position and support informed decision-making.  
The Director leads the Museum’s annual budgeting and financial planning processes, monitors financial performance against the Board-approved budget, and works with department heads to ensure that spending remains within approved limits. The Director proactively identifies financial risks, cash flow pressures, and emerging variances, and recommends timely corrective actions to leadership.  
The Director is accountable for the accuracy, reliability, and timeliness of all financial information; the integrity of the Museum’s accounting operations and internal controls; and compliance with applicable accounting standards, nonprofit regulations, grant requirements, and other financial obligations. The Director fosters a culture of financial accountability, transparency, and compliance across the organization.  
As a key member of the senior administrative team, the Director maintains regular communication with leadership and provides clear, actionable financial reporting and analysis to the Executive Director, Finance Committee, and Board of Trustees.

### **Organizational Structure and Supervision**

The Director of Finance reports to the Executive Director and serves as a member of the Museum’s senior administrative team. The Director works closely with the Executive Director, Board Finance Committee, and department heads to support financial planning, budget accountability, and the Museum’s overall financial stability.  
The Director regularly presents financial results, cash flow forecasts, budget performance, and emerging financial risks and recommendations at Finance Committee and Board of Trustees meetings.  
The Director oversees the Museum’s accounting and finance functions, including internal finance staff and external accounting support, and serves as the primary liaison with auditors, banks, investment advisors, payroll providers, financial consultants, and other financial service providers.  
  
**RESPONSIBILITIES**

### **Accounting & Compliance**

* Administer, manage, and evaluate the Museum’s accounting and financial activities, systems, policies, procedures, and internal controls; ensure financial records are maintained in compliance with organizational policy and GAAP.
* Ensure compliance with GAAP, federal and New York State nonprofit financial and reporting requirements, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs and Cultural Institutions Group obligations, and all applicable government and private grant agreements, including restricted-fund accounting, financial reporting, and audit requirements.

**The gap no one has filled**
Every complex system in America has a profession whose job it is to be your trusted guide. You have a lawyer for legal. An accountant for taxes. A financial advisor for your money. Healthcare, a trillion-dollar industry that's arguably the most complex and touches every single family, leaves us on our own.
  
  
99% of care happens when someone steps outside the four walls of a doctor's office. Hera is creating a new profession in healthcare to fill that gap: the Hero, a dedicated senior care expert for your family. Our Heroes educate, coordinate, and advocate for the most vulnerable population in the healthcare system. We’re covered by insurance, so we can serve every family in America.
  
  
**Building the most trusted interface of healthcare**
We are in the business of trust.
  
  
We're designing for the most emotionally charged moments of our customers' lives; the bar isn't just delight, it's trust. Hera's brand promise is simple: care worthy of our parents. This promise is our moat.
  
  
It's what physicians refer to, families buy, what Heroes deliver, and what the product must unlock and enforce at every touchpoint.
  
  
**Our product challenge**
The bottleneck isn't demand, it's supply. There aren't enough experts to serve every family who needs us. To scale to all of America, we have to unbundle expertise from the human so that anyone who can foster human connection can become a Hero.
  
  
The problem is that this expertise is tribal knowledge. One social worker knows how to expedite Medicaid in New York, another knows which home-visiting PT families actually love. It's trapped in people's heads.
  
  
To solve this, our platform captures every interaction and turns it into compounding intelligence that makes every user smarter. Think Waymo: expert humans do the driving today, and every mile they log trains the system so that tomorrow, anyone — even with zero healthcare background — can perform like a 20-year veteran. The hard part is building a system that knows what to trust, what's gone stale, what's local versus universal, and how to surface the right insight at the right moment. Every Hero we hire, every market we open, every payer we contract with and every program we bill under is a bet with a cost and a return that either compounds or doesn’t. You’ll turn those bets into numbers we trust, then go out and move the numbers.
  
  
You’ll bring the analytical rigor of a seasoned financier and the ethos of a strong operator: surgical execution, relentless truth seeking and an obsession with greatness. You'll work through hard tradeoffs in the business and then go make it happen.

We’re Teva, a leading innovative biopharmaceutical company, enabled by a world-class generics business. Whether it’s innovating in the fields of neuroscience and immunology or delivering high-quality medicine worldwide, we’re dedicated to addressing patients’ needs now and in the future. Here, you will be part of a high-performing, inclusive culture that values fresh thinking and collaboration. You'll have the room to grow, the flexibility to balance life with work, and the opportunity to better health worldwide, together.
  
  
**Our Team, Your Impact**
The Director of Value and Access Strategy is a key member of the Biosimilar Value and Access Strategy team, reporting to the Senior Director, Value and Access Strategy. The Director is responsible for leading, developing, and implementing biosimilar product access strategies aligned with achieving brand objectives while minimizing GTN impact.
  
  
The Director, in collaboration with the Senior Director and Teva’s V&A Strategic Pricing Team, will develop ecosystem wide pricing and contracting strategies that align with biosimilar commercialization plans and support achievement of net sales goals. The individual in this role will lead cross-functional collaboration with internal stakeholders to meet strategic value and access objectives in support of brand objectives. The Director is responsible for leading all aspects of biosimilar value and access strategy, including pricing strategy, contracting strategy, monitoring contract performance, ASP/GTN management, competitive analysis, launch planning, payer marketing resources, organizational communication, annual operating plans, budget management, and vendor alliance management. Pricing and contracting strategy impact patient access to Teva biosimilars, product ASP, GTN, net sales, gross profit, and overall brand performance. Therefore, financial acumen and ensuring pricing and contracting strategies optimize access for Teva biosimilars and minimize impact on GTN/ASP are key responsibilities of the Director.
  
  
This is a hybrid position working from Teva’s Parsippany headquarters.

* Value & Access Strategy: Development and execution of pricing and contracting strategies to optimize access for Teva’s biosimilar products and gain a competitive advantage where possible, while also minimizing GTN impact and maximizing net selling price (NSP)/net sales.
* Strategic pricing and contracting: Work with Value & Access Analytics, Finance, and Forecasting teams to ensure that pricing and contract strategies account for contracting across the healthcare ecosystem, including payer, providers, pharmacies, distribution, hospitals, government entities, and affordability program costs. The Director is accountable for impacts to best price, government rebates and penalties, ASP, AMP, most favored nation agreements, and other terms that have financial implications.

* Budget management: Lead cross-functional partners to conduct comprehensive financial analysis and forecasting of product volumes and net sales resulting from contracting strategies. Monitor and manage budgets for agency work on promotional assets and consulting services.
* Data analysis: Develop and monitor V&A performance goals related to the business outcomes expected from pricing and contracting strategies.

**What is Kalshi?**
-------------------

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

* Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.
* Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

----------------

Your role will push you to be close to customers and to bring creative solutions to their needs, including the ones they’re not aware of.

* Refine and improve our understanding of our customers and their needs, including those they’re not aware of
* Apply an experimental and iterative mindset to design and solution exploration

* A compelling portfolio showcasing your ability to craft delightful product experiences (show us!)
* Deeply in love with your craft, obsessive over design details, and focused on excellence in execution.
* Strong customer intuition and consumer sensibility

Oliver Wyman, a Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) business, is a management consulting firm driven by deep industry insight, bold innovation, and a collaborative approach that cuts through complexity to help organizations navigate their most defining transformative moments.
  
  
For more information, visit oliverwyman.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.
  
  
**Job Overview**
Oliver Wyman is seeking a Senior FP&A Analyst to join our Corporate FP&A team within the Office of the CFO. This role will play a key part in running and improving the day-to-day Corporate FP&A function, with responsibility for core financial reporting, forecasting, close analysis, executive reporting, and financial analytics.
  
  
A key focus of the role will be to take ownership of recurring FP&A processes and continuously improve how they are performed. The Senior Analyst will use data, automation, BI tools, and emerging AI capabilities to reduce manual effort, strengthen data quality, and improve the speed and quality of financial insight.
  
  
As core processes become more efficient, the role will also support broader CFO priorities, including scenario analysis, strategic planning, margin improvement, finance transformation, and other high-impact initiatives.
  
  
The ideal candidate combines strong FP&A fundamentals with an ownership mindset, excellent analytical skills, and a genuine interest in how Finance operates.
  
  
This is a hybrid role requiring 3 days per week at our midtown NYC location. There is no option to be fully remote.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
**Own Core FP&A Processes**

* Take ownership of monthly and quarterly financial reporting, including the Flash process, consolidated P&L analysis, revenue, headcount, compensation and benefits, and other key performance measures.
* Support the month-end close process, including variance analysis, reconciliations, investigation of unusual items, and coordination with Controllership and other Finance teams.
* Manage recurring reporting timelines, follow-ups, and issue resolution with limited supervision.
* Prepare clear financial commentary explaining key performance drivers, risks, opportunities, and emerging trends.
* Ensure reporting outputs are accurate, timely, and consistent across financial systems and management reporting.

**Forecasting, Budgeting & Planning**

* Support and increasingly own components of the annual budget, periodic forecasting, and rolling forecast processes.
* Partner with Corporate and Regional FP&A teams to consolidate inputs, challenge assumptions, and understand key changes in financial outlook.
* Develop driver-based analyses and scenario models incorporating revenue, headcount, utilization, compensation, and other key business assumptions.
* Support longer-range planning and sensitivity analysis for management decision-making.

**Executive Reporting & Business Partnership**

* Prepare financial analysis, commentary, and presentation materials for the CFO, Global FP&A leadership, and other senior stakeholders.
* Translate detailed financial information into concise, decision-useful insights and clear management narratives.

Our Deloitte Strategy & Transactions team helps guide clients through their most critical moments and transformational initiatives. description:
**Vice President, Technology & Digital Transformation**

**Confidential Executive Search | Mission-Driven Nonprofit Organization**

A mission-driven nonprofit organization is conducting a confidential search for a visionary and hands-on technology leader to transform technology from a support function into a strategic organizational asset.

This position is intended to elevate technology to the same strategic level as finance, human resources, and legal within the organization. The Vice President will serve as a member of the senior leadership team and help shape organizational strategy, innovation, growth, and operational effectiveness through technology, data, cybersecurity, and digital transformation.

**Position Overview**

The Vice President, Technology & Digital Transformation will lead the organization's technology strategy, operations, cybersecurity, data architecture, and modernization efforts.

The organization currently operates within a complex technology environment that includes multiple databases, legacy systems, custom-built platforms, outsourced cybersecurity resources, and a variety of stand-alone systems developed over time.

The Vice President will be responsible for developing and executing a technology roadmap that modernizes this environment while ensuring reliable day-to-day operations.

This role requires both strategic leadership and hands-on execution. The successful candidate will be expected to participate in executive planning and organizational visioning while serving as the internal owner of technology decisions, priorities, investments, and outcomes.

The organization will continue to utilize specialized consultants and vendors where appropriate. However, this position will be accountable for technology strategy, cybersecurity oversight, systems architecture, vendor management, and technology transformation across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership**

* Serve as the organization's principal advisor on technology, cybersecurity, data, and digital transformation.
* Participate as a member of the senior leadership team.
* Develop and execute a multi-year technology strategy aligned with organizational goals.
* Partner with program, operations, finance, HR, and legal leadership to identify opportunities to improve services, efficiency, decision-making, and organizational capacity through technology.
* Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend strategic investments.

**Technology Modernization**

**Lead major initiatives including:**

* Database consolidation and modernization.
* CRM selection, implementation, and optimization.
* Website redevelopment.
* Learning management system implementation and integration.
* Data governance and reporting improvements.
* Business process automation and workflow redesign.
* Development of scalable technology infrastructure that supports future growth.

**Information Technology Operations**

* Oversee all technology systems, infrastructure, applications, and support services.
* Manage Microsoft 365 and related cloud-based technologies.
* Supervise the Technology Support Specialist.
* Serve as the escalation point for complex technical issues.
* Ensure reliable, secure, and efficient technology operations across the organization.
* Develop technology policies, standards, and documentation.
* Manage technology budgets, vendors, contracts, and service providers.
* Ensure the organization receives timely and effective day-to-day technical support, including troubleshooting hardware, software, network, and user access issues.
* Establish service standards and processes to ensure employees have the technology resources and support needed to perform their jobs.
* Oversee employee onboarding and offboarding technology requirements, including account provisioning, access management, equipment assignment, and deactivation.
* Monitor recurring technical issues and identify opportunities to improve systems, service delivery, and the employee technology experience.

**Cybersecurity & Risk Management**

* Lead the organization's cybersecurity strategy and risk management efforts.
* Manage relationships with external cybersecurity providers and consultants.
* Oversee risk assessments, incident response planning, business continuity, and disaster recovery.
* Ensure compliance with applicable security, privacy, contractual, and regulatory requirements.
* Build organizational awareness and capacity around cybersecurity best practices.

**Data & Organizational Intelligence**

* Develop and implement an enterprise data strategy.
* Improve data quality, governance, reporting, and analytics.
* Support grant reporting, program evaluation, and organizational performance management.
* Help leadership leverage data to inform strategic decision-making.

**Artificial Intelligence & Emerging Technologies**

* Develop and implement an organizational strategy for the responsible adoption and use of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
* Identify opportunities to leverage AI to improve operational efficiency, automate business processes, reduce administrative workloads, and enhance organizational effectiveness.
* Evaluate, recommend, and oversee the implementation of any needed AI platforms, tools, and applications that support organizational priorities.
* Establish AI governance policies and standards addressing data privacy, information security, confidentiality, accuracy, intellectual property, and appropriate human oversight.
* Partner with executive leadership, Legal, HR, and other departments to assess AI opportunities, manage risks, and establish appropriate guidelines for organizational use.
* Lead organizational adoption of AI through staff education, training, and change management.
* Monitor developments in AI and emerging technologies and recommend opportunities for innovation and improved organizational performance.

#### **Who We Are**

Founded in 1958 as a children's reading group, East Harlem Tutorial Program (EHTP) has grown into a multi-faceted education nonprofit with the mission of preparing children in East Harlem with the academic skills, strength of character, and emotional well-being to excel academically, lead in their communities, and realize their best possible selves. The organization currently comprises two public charter schools that serve approximately 1,000 students in grades PreK through 12th grade, as well as afterschool and summer programs, wraparound services for families, and a teaching residency. Together, these programs provide East Harlem youth with a holistic educational experience that includes rigorous and supportive school-day instruction, as well as opportunities to explore extracurricular interests, build social emotional skills, and develop pride in their identities and community. This well-rounded approach prepares our students not only to gain admission to the colleges of their choice, but to thrive on college campuses, persist to graduation, and pursue meaningful careers. We remain deeply committed to the East Harlem community, partnering with our parents and local leaders to ensure that our work is responsive to community needs and aspirations.

In the last two years, EHTP has focused on improving the educational experience at our Scholars Academies, resulting in remarkable growth in academic outcomes across all subject areas and grade levels. We are now poised to take our work to the next level, realizing our vision for academic excellence and ensuring all of our scholars graduate from high school college and career-ready.

We're looking for a fundraising leader who has personally closed major gifts, grown a donor base, and led a team, to guide EHTP's fundraising strategy and build broad, lasting philanthropic support. The Chief Development Officer will be supported by a committed donor base and a strong, stable board with a history of successful fundraising, including two capital campaigns that funded the construction of state-of-the art facilities for both our lower and upper school campuses. Building on this solid foundation, the CDO will be charged with expanding EHTP's philanthropic reach, identifying and cultivating sustainable relationships with new individuals, foundations, and corporate partners.

EHTP currently raises about $4.5 million a year in private support for two interconnected organizations, East Harlem Tutorial Program and East Harlem Scholars Academies, which share a CEO and development team. The Chief Development Officer will lead fundraising across both, carry a personal portfolio of major donors, and lead the Campaign to Build Excellence, a $3 million initiative to fund investments to accelerate academic outcomes and post-secondary success. Leading a lean three-person development team and serving as close partner to the CEO and integral member of her cabinet, the CDO must be both a strategic organizational leader and a hands-on fundraiser who will do the work while building the capacity of others.

The successful Chief Development Officer will:

* Expand our major gifts pipeline, strengthening donor acquisition, stewardship, and retention.

* Elevate the donor experience and fundraising outcomes of two signature fundraising events each year.

* Partner and build the capacity of the CEO and other key leaders to support revenue generation, building a culture of philanthropy across the organization.

**About the Company**

At Flow, we’re reimagining what it means to live, work, and connect. More than just a real estate company, Flow is a brand, a technology platform, and an operations ecosystem spanning condominiums, hotels, multifamily residences, and office spaces. We’re building a new kind of living experience: one that’s flexible, connected, and designed to create genuine community and real value for the people who call Flow home.

**About the Role**

We’re looking for a sharp, hands-on Assistant Controller to join our fast-growing Accounting team. Reporting to the Corporate Controller, you'll play a critical role in scaling our controllership function while ensuring accuracy, compliance, and operational excellence across the board. You’ll help lead month-end close, strengthen internal controls, support audits, and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to drive insight and accountability across the business.

This is a great opportunity for someone who thrives in a high-growth environment and wants to help build a world-class accounting org from the inside out. Also, we believe employees are better together. Every position at Flow has an onsite or in-office requirement.

### **What You’ll Do**

* Lead the month-end close process, including preparation of account reconciliations, journal entries, and internal management reports
* Partner with the Corporate Controller to develop and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and documentation that scale with the business
* Draft GAAP-compliant technical accounting memos that clearly communicate complex concepts and their operational impact
* Support reporting integrity by working with FP&A to ensure records align with key business dimensions (e.g., departments, vendors, business units)
* Manage and maintain financial system dimensions and reporting structures in our ERP (Sage Intacct experience is a plus)
* Help enhance and implement internal controls for both existing and evolving processes
* Support external audits by organizing requests, managing timelines, and offering clear documentation and commentary
* Pitch in on team development, cross-functional initiatives, and special projects as needed

### **What You Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Accounting, with 8–10 years of relevant experience (a mix of public accounting and in-house experience preferred)
* Solid foundation in US GAAP (IFRS experience a plus) and experience preparing or reviewing financial statements
* Strong leadership and interpersonal skills—you know how to collaborate, influence, and bring clarity to complex topics
* Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and communication (both written and verbal)
* Experience working across multiple legal entities and ownership structures
* Advanced Excel skills, with bonus points for Python and SQL exposure
* CPA strongly preferred, but not required
* Experience with a modern ERP system—Sage Intacct or similar preferred

### **Why You’ll Love Working Here**

* You’ll join a team that values precision, pragmatism, and partnership. We take pride in getting the details right, moving fast without cutting corners, and building systems that last. You’ll have a voice, real ownership, and a chance to shape how accounting supports our continued growth.

title: Director of Finance & Business Operations
description:
Speks is a fast-growing, New York-based product design company creating premium sensory products for teens and adults. Our products are sold globally through major retailers including Target, Walmart and Barnes & Noble, specialty stores, international distributors, Amazon and our own website.

As we continue to scale, we're building the financial and operational infrastructure needed to support our next stage of growth.

**The Role**

We're looking for an experienced, entrepreneurial leader to oversee Finance and Business Operations at Speks.

You'll own financial strategy, cash flow, working capital, profitability, accounting oversight and business operations. Our business involves significant investments in overseas manufacturing and inventory, making strong financial planning and capital management essential to our growth.

You'll lead an existing team, including internal business operations staff and external accounting and bookkeeping resources, with the opportunity to build out the department as we grow.

This is a leadership role, not a bookkeeping position. We're looking for someone who can manage people, build systems, solve problems and provide the financial discipline needed to scale a fast-growing consumer business.

We're hiring at the Director level, with flexibility for an experienced candidate to join as VP of Finance & Business Operations.

**What You'll Own**

**Financial Strategy & Cash Management**

* Own cash flow forecasting, working capital planning and banking relationships.
* Develop funding strategies for major retail programs, overseas production and inventory investments.
* Manage credit facilities, financing opportunities and customer credit policies.

**Accounting & Financial Reporting**

* Oversee the accounting team, external bookkeepers and monthly financial close.
* Ensure accurate financial reporting, inventory accounting, landed costs and reconciliations across sales channels.
* Manage outside accountants, tax compliance and financial controls.

**Budgeting & Profitability**

* Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts and financial planning.
* Build visibility into margins and profitability by channel, customer and product.
* Partner with merchandising, sales and planning on pricing, inventory investments and major program decisions.
* Provide clear, actionable financial reporting to the CEO and leadership team.

**Receivables & Payables**

* Oversee invoicing, collections, vendor payments and cash management processes.
* Improve management of retailer deductions, chargebacks and customer payment terms.
* Establish clear financial approval procedures and accountability.

**Business Operations**

* Lead the Business Operations team, overseeing company administration, insurance, benefits, payroll coordination, vendor contracts and office operations.
* Manage legal operations and outside counsel.
* Build scalable policies, processes and internal controls.
* Identify opportunities to improve efficiency through technology, automation and AI.

**Who We're Looking For**

* 10+ years of experience in finance and business operations, including senior financial leadership experience.
* Strong background in consumer products, toys, hardgoods or another inventory-intensive business.
* Experience managing cash flow, inventory financing, overseas manufacturing costs and major retail customer relationships.
* Proven ability to lead accounting and business operations teams, build financial processes and manage external partners.
* Strong financial planning, budgeting, reporting and analytical skills.
* Familiarity with QuickBooks Online, ERP systems and financial modeling. Cin7 experience is a plus.
* Entrepreneurial, resourceful and comfortable operating in a fast-moving, growing business.
* Commercially minded, with the ability to balance financial discipline and growth.
* A natural problem-solver who takes ownership, builds strong teams and gets things done without unnecessary bureaucracy.
* We value practical experience, sound judgment and demonstrated results over traditional corporate credentials.

**Why Join Speks?**

* Work directly with the CEO and play a meaningful role in the company's growth.
* Build and lead the finance and business operations functions of a rapidly scaling consumer brand.
* Have real ownership over financial strategy, systems, processes and your team.
* Work across global manufacturing, major retail programs, international distribution and e-commerce.

**Compensation:**
$180–200k base salary, plus performance-based bonus and benefits.

**Location:**
Full-time, in-office in Midtown Manhattan.

description:
**Target Start:** January 2027

**About Us**
------------

Dashly is a fraud intelligence startup that uses data across employers, insurers, contractors, and open source intelligence to fight fraud in injury claims. We expose fraud networks that cost Americans billions of dollars annually, slow commercial development, and erode trust in blue-collar industries.

Backed by Mosaic GP, Altai Ventures, and Remarkable Ventures, with a $5.8M seed round.

**About the Role**
------------------

Fraud in injury claims is rarely one person acting alone. Organized claim fraud is often run by networks: groups of associated people acting together through a pattern of related claims over time. The cost falls on carriers, contractors, and the industries that depend on fair claims. The evidence is public but fragmented across dockets, deposition transcripts, claim files, and social media.

We investigate organized fraud enterprises, not isolated claims: formal or informal groups of claimants, and the counsel, providers, and associates around them, linked by shared addresses, phone numbers, employers, and narratives. We document the structure of organized fraud: the enterprise, each member's association with it, a pattern of related conduct, how long that conduct continues, and its reach across state lines. Our work gives clients and their counsel evidence for fraud litigation.

As a Senior Technical OSINT Investigator, you will lead high-impact OSINT investigations and own the design and automation of workflows that underpin our due diligence operations. You’ll drive the creation of robust tooling, standard operating procedures, and playbooks that convert investigative expertise into repeatable, scalable methods for both analysts and AI agents. You will integrate OSINT, licensed, and public records data sources via API, and maintain detection quality across all stages of analysis. Your investigative reports will serve as the foundation for our clients’ litigation efforts.

This role is ideal for an experienced OSINT or technical investigations professional passionate about applying advanced investigative techniques to solve complex fraud challenges. You will collaborate closely with product, engineering, and operations teams to continually enhance investigative quality and operational speed.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Lead OSINT investigations and due diligence operations targeting organized fraud enterprises, designing automated workflows for scalable execution by analysts and AI agents.
* Use link analysis to map relationships and pinpoint critical inconsistencies between claimants, legal counsel, service providers, and other associated actors.
* Build, ship, and maintain internal tooling, automated pipelines, and AI-driven workflows utilizing coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, or equivalents) and custom scripting for data collection, ingestion, and integration.
* Own detection quality: define precision, recall, and false-positive and false-negative metrics against analyst-confirmed accounts, and use them to tune workflows.
* Write the standard operating procedures, playbooks, and investigative briefs that turn tradecraft into repeatable methods.
* Partner with engineering, product, and operations leadership to continuously refine systems and optimize performance.
* Mentor junior analysts, providing instruction in advanced investigative techniques, quality assurance, and leveraging AI-assisted analysis.
* Personally conduct the most complex investigations, delivering thorough and actionable, evidence-based reports for litigation purposes.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Experience building with AI coding agents or CLI-based AI development tools (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, or equivalents), and proficiency in Python or a similar language to automate investigative workflows.
* 3+ years of experience in intelligence analysis, OSINT, or investigations, ideally in a government, military, law enforcement, corporate, or insurance investigations setting.
* Demonstrated ability to attribute and trace a person across public records, court filings, social media, and other open sources, and to explain the confidence behind each match.
* Experience designing tooling, standard operating procedures, playbooks, and training frameworks that scale across teams.
* Strong OSINT and due diligence skills, with clear, concise reporting for both executive stakeholders and technical partners.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* SQL for querying, analyzing, and extracting insights from relational databases.
* Experience integrating OSINT, licensed, and public-records data sources through REST APIs and working with structured data.
* Experience defining detection-quality metrics (precision, recall, false positives) and evaluation sets.

**Role Purpose**

The Accounting Manager is responsible for the accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of the company’s financial operations. This role leads the monthly close process, oversees accounts payable and accounts receivable performance, manages credit and collections activity, maintains general ledger structure, and supports budgeting and forecasting initiatives.

Travers is a product distribution business with significant physical inventory across multiple locations. Experience in an inventory-intensive environment is highly valued—the right candidate will be comfortable with inventory costing methods, cost-of-goods-sold accounting, gross margin analysis, cycle count reconciliation, inventory reserves, and the interplay between purchasing, warehousing, and the general ledger.

Strong process discipline, internal control awareness, and team leadership are critical. Financial accuracy directly impacts cash flow, vendor relationships, compliance, and executive visibility into company performance.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Financial Close & Reporting**

* Lead and manage the monthly and periodic close process, coordinating timelines and reviewing deliverables
* Review and approve bank reconciliations and key balance sheet reconciliations
* Oversee journal entries, accruals, prepaids, and fixed asset accounting
* Ensure subledgers properly reconcile to the general ledger
* Produce internal financial reports including cash reporting and management summaries
* Maintain audit-ready financial records and documentation

**Inventory Accounting & Cost Management**

* Partner with operations and purchasing to ensure inventory is accurately valued in the general ledger
* Oversee COGS accounting, landed cost allocation, and gross margin reporting
* Support and reconcile cycle count programs; investigate and resolve inventory variances
* Maintain inventory reserve calculations (slow-moving, obsolete, shrinkage)
* Collaborate on standard cost updates and analyze cost-to-actual variances

**Accounts Payable Oversight & Working Capital Management**

* Supervise Accounts Payable operations to ensure timely and accurate invoice processing
* Monitor AP service levels and vendor payment timing to balance relationships and working capital goals
* Ensure vendor terms are optimized, including early-pay discounts and rebate tracking
* Resolve escalated vendor and internal AP issues; maintain strong internal controls within AP

**Accounts Receivable, Credit & Collections**

* Supervise the AR/cash posting clerk and credit & collections staff
* Ensure accurate and timely cash application and customer account reconciliation
* Oversee credit evaluation processes for new and existing customers
* Monitor collections activity, aging trends, and DSO; escalate delinquent accounts as needed
* Maintain bad debt reserves and write-off procedures in accordance with company policy
* Partner with sales and customer service to resolve billing disputes and payment issues

**General Ledger Governance**

* Own and maintain the chart of accounts; ensure consistent and appropriate account usage across departments
* Review coding trends, correct misclassifications, and maintain alignment between reporting needs and GL structure
* Ensure data integrity within the ERP and accounting systems

**Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Planning Support**

* Assist department leaders in preparing annual budgets and periodic forecasts
* Conduct variance analysis using historical and trend data
* Support ROI and cost-benefit analysis for business initiatives as needed

**Financial Controls, Compliance & Process Improvement**

* Maintain compliance with accounting policies and internal control standards
* Identify control gaps, process risks, and inefficiencies; standardize and document procedures
* Support audit and tax preparation processes

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Supervise and develop AP, AR, credit & collections, and accounting staff; set clear expectations and provide regular feedback
* Cross-train team members to reduce key-person dependency
* Foster accountability, accuracy, and a service-oriented mindset within the finance team
