About Equi

Equi gives investors the tools to own their financial future. We bring institutional-quality alternative strategies, in hedge funds and private credit, that are hard to get access to, to wealth advisors, family offices and institutions. We build and manage multi-strategy funds and white-labeled funds for some of the best independent multi-family offices and advisory firms in the country, pairing Silicon Valley tech with Wall St expertise.

Our growth is accelerating rapidly. We just launched the largest client in our history, have several more signed or close, and are targeting a multiple of today's assets. We're about ten people, so every hire here shapes a function rather than inheriting one. We hire builders and team players that aren't afraid of taking a high degree of ownership.

The role

You'll own finance and fund operations for the fund complex and the management company, reporting to the CEO. That means the NAV cycle and the reconciliation behind it; capital calls, distributions, redemptions and onboarding; every wire and the controls around it; budget, treasury, audit and tax; investor reporting; and the setup of every new vehicle.

We own our books. You'll build and run an internal shadow NAV for every vehicle, one we're 100% confident in, and reconcile it against our administrator every cycle. When the numbers disagree, you decide the firm's position, and you hold our administrator, auditor, counsel and banks to a standard. Partners should be checking our work, not telling us what our numbers are.

When something recurring is manual, you build the thing that removes it instead of absorbing it or hiring for it. These agents touch investor money, so the bar is production, not demo: each one is checked against an independent source, has evals that catch a regression when a prompt or model changes, and hands off to a person instead of failing silently. If you can't say how you'd know an agent got something wrong, it doesn't go live.

 - We run our own shadow NAV on every vehicle and trust it fully, every close reconciles it against the administrator, and nothing reaches an investor without your sign-off

 - Our own books: an internal shadow NAV on every vehicle, reconciled against the administrator each cycle, with your final sign-off

 - Fund operations: capital calls, distributions, redemptions, subscriptions and investor onboarding

 - Money movement: cash across operating and fund accounts, and approval authority on every wire

 - Corporate finance: fund expense budget and allocation, burn and runway, board reporting, payroll and benefits

 - Audit, tax and compliance: counterpart to the auditor and tax preparer, working with our compliance partner

 - Launches: the financial setup of each new vehicle, with outside counsel on structure and documents

 - Investor service: reporting that goes out on time, and fast, honest answers to investors and advisers
 - The provider network: administrator, auditor, tax preparer, counsel, prime brokers and banks, held to a written standard
Who you are

You've built or run a shadow NAV, and you find the error in a draft NAV before anyone else does.
 - A builder: you've shipped agents and automations, not just used AI. You can tell us what you built in the last six months, what it changed, where it broke, and how you proved it right before trusting it with real numbers.
 - Technical range beyond spreadsheets: coding agents, scripts, no-code automation, small internal apps. You don't need to be an engineer, but you pick up a new tool over a weekend.

 - Fund legal fluency: you've worked closely with fund counsel and know what a PPM, side letter or subscription agreement commits the firm to.
 - Hands-on: you've worked somewhere small enough that you did the work yourself. If the close always belonged to a team two levels down, this isn't the seat.
 - Direct: you close loops, and you tell the CEO plainly when a number is wrong.
Nice to have: layered multi-vehicle structures, offshore vehicles and their audit cycle, ERISA and plan-asset monitoring, or a CPA or legal background (or equivalent depth earned another way).
How we work
Team-first, flat and direct. Ideas win on merit, people argue a position and change their mind when the evidence says so, and nobody stays narrowly in lane when there's an adjacent fire. title: Manager, Strategy & Planning
description:
About Misfits Market: 
 Misfits Market is a mission-driven, high-growth startup dedicated to reducing food waste and making shopping for sustainable, high-quality groceries easier and more affordable. We deliver organic produce, high-quality meats and seafood, plant-based proteins, dairy, bakery, wine, and other grocery items to nearly every zip code in 48 states at up to 30 percent off traditional grocery store prices. In 2022, Misfits Market acquired sustainable e-grocer Imperfect Foods and now leverages its in-house transportation network to deliver directly to consumers with one of the most carbon-efficient grocery delivery models on the market. By tackling inefficiencies in the food system, our passionate and motivated team of problem solvers helps save an average of 500,000 pounds of food per week from waste or lesser outcomes, with an all-time savings of 190+ million pounds of food. 
 As Misfits we support our customers and mission by embracing our core values of: 
 Prioritizing our Customers                              
 Doing more with less 
 Thinking Differently          
 Respecting one another                              
 Moving deliberately and quickly                    
 Taking initiative and delivering  
 About the Role:  
 The Strategy Planning Manager is responsible for developing, maintaining, and continuously improving the daily and weekly reporting used to make timely business decisions that impact revenue and gross profit.  They are responsible for collecting and summarizing data that will assist the Merchandising organization in both long- and short-range strategic planning, and the development and implementation of new programs. They will become a subject matter expert on processes across the merchandising organization, and, combining this knowledge with their grasp on the business data, be a consultant for other partners on projects including process improvement, strategy development, industry trends, competitive analysis, and company positioning. This role will report to the Director of Strategy Planning.  
 The ideal candidate is a proactive problem solver who thrives on turning complex challenges into organized, impactful solutions. We are looking for an adaptable, collaborative team player with a pragmatic, hands-on approach—someone eager to dive into the details, drive meaningful results, and contribute directly alongside a supportive team and leadership group that actively partners on execution.
 Responsibilities:  
- Assemble, analyze and maintain all data pertinent to creating future sales and gross margin projections (historical sales, market trends, seasonality, customer forecast) 
- Support the Merchandising team in pricing strategy analysis and project managing Category Management execution of pricing initiatives
- Provide support for special projects as well as weekly/monthly business reviews; including compiling and analyzing data from multiple sources and creating templates that outline the data in a cohesive and digestible action oriented format
- Drive continuous improvement in inventory management, assortment planning, pricing, and process building in conjunction with key cross-functional partners
- Communicate regularly with Operations team and help provide analytics that will inform operational initiatives, improving overall efficiency and customer experience 
 Skills and Qualifications:  
- 3-4 years of experience in pricing, financial analysis or analytics experience
- Must have advanced command of Google Sheets and Excel

About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.

 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.
 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.
 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.

title: Senior Financial Analyst, Clinical Finance
description:
About the role 
 We are seeking a Senior Financial Analyst, Clinical Finance to own the financial side of our clinical vendor base, from forecast and contract review through invoice review and monthly accruals. 
 This is a step up for an analyst with 2 to 4 years in biotech or pharma finance who wants to own a process end to end. You will report to our SVP of Finance and partner day to day with Clinical Operations, the accounting team, Legal on contract terms, and our CROs and vendors. The core of the job is knowing what is changing in each trial and making sure the budget, forecast and accruals keep pace. At Pathos, that work does not run on manual spreadsheets and inbox triage. You will use AI agents and automation to build repeatable processes that reduce errors, improve accuracy and surface insights we would otherwise miss. 
 What You Will Do 
 Clinical Spend Forecasting 
 ●      Build and own the clinical trial forecast by vendor, study and cost category (CRO services, pass through costs, site grants, lab, technology, imaging, IRB). 
 ●      Hold a regular dialogue with Clinical Operations to capture changes as they happen: enrollment pace, site activation, protocol amendments, scope changes and timeline shifts. 
 ●      Translate each trial change into its cost and timing impact, and keep forecasts and estimates on the latest plan, not the one in the original contract. 
 ●      Produce the clinical inputs to the annual budget, quarterly reforecasts and cash runway models. 
 Vendor Spend and Invoice Review 
 ●      Maintain a tracker for every clinical vendor that matches each invoice line to its MSA, SOW, work order and executed change orders, and tracks remaining contract value by category. 
 ●      Support the clinical AP process: track incoming invoices in our AP platform, tie them to their POs and study, catch duplicates, and route them to Clinical Operations for review. 
 ●      Review vendor billing by hours, units, milestones and pass through costs against the contract and real study progress, and flag resource use that looks out of scope, overstaffed or ahead of the work before invoices are approved. 
 ●      Track CRO prefunded deposits and site grant funds: what has been prepaid, applied and credited back. 
 ●      Keep a running exceptions log and escalate each item for resolution with the vendor or a Pathos decision. 
 Actuals Versus Forecast 
 ●      Close the loop each month: compare invoiced and accrued spend to forecast by vendor and category, and explain the variances. 
 ●      Keep the clinical spend dashboard current and reconciled to Pathos billing and accounting platforms. 
 ●      Prepare monthly spend, burn and variance reporting for the SVP of Finance and Clinical Operations leadership. 
 Clinical Procurement 
 ●      Support the finance side of contracting: review SOW and change order budgets, compare pricing and rate cards to prior work, flag issues for the SVP of Finance, and confirm budget availability before signature. 
 ●      Provide vendor, study and budget details for purchase order setup in Bill.com. 
 Clinical Accruals 
 ●      Prepare the monthly clinical accrual for each vendor, built from vendor reported work, unit and milestone data, site activity and Clinical Operations input, for review by the SVP of Finance. 
 ●      Maintain accrual and prepaid schedules that support the accounting team’s journal entries and reclasses, and reconcile them to subsequent invoices. 
 ●      Support the annual audit and investor diligence with clear, documented clinical expense support. 
 Who You Are 
 Required Qualifications 
 ●      Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics or a related field. 
 ●      2 to 4 years as a financial analyst at a biotech, pharma company or CRO, with direct exposure to R&D or clinical trial costs across multiple studies. 
 ●      Working knowledge of how clinical trials are contracted and billed: MSAs, SOWs, change orders, pass through costs, site payments and prefunded deposits. 
 ●      Experience building forecasts and variance analyses. 
 ●      Understanding of accrual accounting and month end close. You can build an accrual from operational data with documented support. 
 ●      Advanced Excel: you build models others can follow, audit and update. 
 ●      A strong interest in using AI tools and automation in daily work, with examples of workflows you have streamlined or rebuilt to cut manual effort and errors. 
 ●      The confidence to question a vendor invoice and the judgment to work collaboratively with Clinical Operations. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 ●      Hands on clinical accrual ownership for one or more studies. 
 ●      Experience with QuickBooks Online and Bill.com, or similar ERP and AP tools. 
 ●      Exposure to oncology trials. 
 ●      Experience on a small finance team where you covered several roles. 
 ●      CPA progress or MBA coursework. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 In your first year: 
 ●      Within 90 days, every active vendor has a current tracker reconciled to its contract, the GL and the spend dashboard. 
 ●      No overrun reaches an invoice unflagged, and trial changes show up in the forecast and accruals the same month. 
 ●      Clinical accruals close each month with documented support and no material true ups at audit. 
 Location 
 This is a hybrid role based in our New York City office, with in-person attendance on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. 
 Drug development shouldn’t be guesswork, not when patients are waiting. 
 Pathos is building a next-generation biotech with AI at the core. Not as a feature, but as the operating system for how medicines get developed. We believe most drugs don't fail because the science was wrong. They fail because they were tested in the wrong patients, with the wrong assumptions, in trials that couldn't answer the real question: who benefits, and why? 
 [...]  How We Build 
 [...]

description:
ABOUT BASELAYER 
 Every business in America needs a bank account to exist. The system that decides whether they're real, who's behind them, and whether they're a risk, runs on infrastructure from the 1980s. We're rebuilding that layer from scratch.
 Baselayer is the identity layer for institutions across the United States: the most complete business graph in America and every human tied to it. We fuse public records, IRS data, sanctions lists, web signals, and fraud telemetry from 2,200+ financial institutions into a single graph that resolves any business and the humans behind it in milliseconds. The legacy credit bureaus took 50 years to build something that gets 60% match rates. We've built something that gets 98% in under two years.
 Today we're trusted by over 20% of financial institutions in America including FIS, Rho, Socure and top five US banks. But the graph is becoming infrastructure for anyone who needs to know if a business is real and worth trusting: gig platforms, marketplaces, AI companies, and commerce infrastructure at scale.
 Trust is the substrate of every financial transaction. We're rebuilding it.
 ABOUT THE TEAM 
 AI agents are starting to transact: opening accounts, buying services, moving money on behalf of the businesses and people behind them. Every one of those transactions has a counterparty asking the question banks have always asked: who am I dealing with, and can I trust them? Today's identity infrastructure wasn't built to answer it at agent speed.
 The Agentic Economy team is extending Baselayer's business graph into the trust layer for agentic commerce: verifiable credentials that bind an agent to the verified business and human behind it, a registry counterparties can query in real time, and verification APIs that plug into the networks, platforms, and protocols where agent transactions happen.
 We run like a startup inside a startup: a small senior team led by our GM of Agentic Economy, working directly with payment networks, banks, wallet providers, and agent platforms. The category is being defined right now; the standards, seats, and infrastructure decisions of the next 18 months will be consequential for a decade.
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 We are looking for a Finance & Operations Analyst to be the Swiss Army knife of our Operations & Finance team. You will own the numbers — month-end close, accounting, and FP&A — and you will also own smaller tasks that keep a fast-growing startup running, from office logistics to getting a new teammate's laptop set up.

You will see the entire business: how revenue is recognized, where money goes, what it costs to grow, and where the process is still held together with duct tape. - Produce recurring management and board-level reporting on revenue, burn, runway, and departmental spend
- Turn ambiguous questions into clear analysis: what is this costing us, what is driving the variance, and what should we do about it
 Business Operations

- Own vendor and software spend management, including renewals and contracts
- Support compliance and corporate housekeeping in partnership with Legal and Compliance including annual SOC2, penetration testing, business insurance and more

- Work with BI tooling to provide valuable insights to internal key players
 Accounting & Month-End Close 
- Assist with the month-end close process end to end — journal entries, accruals, prepaids, and account reconciliations

- Partner with our outside accountants and tax advisors on close support, year-end, and compliance filings

And the job of creating better internet is never done - so we’re growing! Our team is committed to building a place where people who want to make a difference can grow their careers and find their spot to belong.
 The application window will be open until at least November 5th, 2026 . This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the specified date. 
 This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. 
 Role Description: 
 We are seeking a Call Center Vendor Manager to establish, manage, and optimize outsourced operations supporting specialty and general customer service groups. In this critical Individual Contributor (IC) role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end performance lifecycle: from architecting new workflows, defining KPIs to driving daily execution and continuous improvement. You will leverage data analysis, performance dashboards, and insightful reporting to hold vendors accountable for meeting KPIs. In addition, you will drive an improved customer experience through  identifying and resolving process gaps, developing outage management strategies, contributing significantly to system design and migration, and creating impactful agent scripting/training. Your ability to design programs from scratch, build relationships within gFiber and at the vendor will be key to driving process improvements. You will need to be a master story teller translating complex business problems into simple actionable insights.
 In this role, you’ll:  
- Drive customer experience improvements by designing, launching, and managing vendor operations; define end-to-end workflows, workforce requirements, routing strategies, and KPIs to ensure efficient call handling and productivity.
- Develop and implement pilot programs, agent scripts, and training modules; analyze vendor performance data, CSAT, and customer insights to identify trends, address process gaps, and drive continuous improvement in service quality and customer experience, including specific protocols for customer outages.
- Proactively identify inefficiencies in existing processes and lead improvement initiatives; leverage a system-design mindset to contribute significantly to the transition from legacy systems to new platforms, designing and implementing solutions from the ground up.
- Create, maintain, and evolve performance dashboards and reporting mechanisms; analyze data to visualize trends, measure vendor productivity against KPIs, and deliver actionable weekly insights to leadership and vendor partners.
- Lead regular vendor performance reviews, presenting data-driven insights and strategic recommendations to manage relationships effectively, ensure accountability towards achieving operational targets, and align on performance management strategies.
- Participate in an "On Call" rotation every 6 weeks, including nights, weekends, and holidays.
 At a minimum we’d like you to have: 
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
- 5 years of experience in Internet Service Provider (ISP) operations.
- 7 years of experience in Call Center Vendor Management within Customer Service contact centers
- Experience manipulating and analyzing large data sets in spreadsheets (Google Sheets , Creating Dashboards, pulling data from SQL tables) to performance manage results
- Experience managing cross-functional and cross-regional teams in Project Management, Customer Service, Process Quality, and Process Optimization
- Ability to travel 25% of the time domestically and to nearshore locations.
 It’s preferred if you have:    
- 5 years of experience managing a team within an ISP (Internet Service Provider) or similar technical industry.
- Experience with designing and implementing workflows, process improvements and systems or tools to work with external parties
- Proven ability to drive back-office efficiency, monitoring, and KPI compliance.
- Experience with influencing internal and partner organizations working with engineering, field operations,  shared services, customer service, sales support in developing value propositions.
- Problem-solving skills, with the ability to build and maintain capacity and budget
- Experience in contract negotiations
- Ability to adapt to change quickly and effectively while operating in a fast-paced, constantly evolving team environment; self-starter with an analytical mindset and ability to work independently on multiple initiatives at the same time

 At CHANEL, we are focused on creating an inclusive culture that nurtures personal growth, contributing to collective progress. We believe the uniqueness of each individual increases the diversity, complementarity, and effectiveness of our teams. We strongly encourage your application, as we value the perspective, experience and potential you could bring to CHANEL.   
 About the role:   
 CHANEL is looking for a Senior Manager, People Analytics, Insights & AI Enablement to join our New York City team. This role sits in the Organizational Development & Effectiveness (OD&E) Center of Excellence within the US People & Organization (P&O/ Human Resources) team. You will enable P&O (HR) to make better, faster, evidence-based decisions through people analytics, insights and the thoughtful use of technology and AI. You will define P&O’s AI needs (in partnership with People Operations), how people insights and foresights are produced and used, and how AI supports the future P&O operating model. This role is a strategist and enabler who turns people data, insights, and AI into business outcomes and a future-fit org.  
 Minimum of 7 years' experience in People Analytics, Human Resources, Process Insights, with recent expertise in Artificial Intelligence.  Hands on experience in Microsoft environment with Power BI, AI Tools, Qualtrics- Employee Survey, etc.   
 What impact you can create at CHANEL:   
- Define the people analytics roadmap and standard dashboards to support people insights across the US— so the same questions are answered the same way, reducing fragmented one-off demand and freeing the team for higher-value, predictive work  
- Translate workforce data into insights and recommended actions, and build predictive, forward-looking models for workforce planning (e.g., retention, capacity, and scenario forecasting)

- Enable self-service analytics for HRBPs and business leaders — with the right guardrails and advance data literacy across P&O  
- Own employee listening and our employee engagement survey (Voices) analytics — turning what people tell us into insight  
- Partner with People Operations to improve data quality and data governance in service of AI integration  
 You are energized by:   
- Turning data into decisions — and data storytelling that moves leaders to act

title: Revenue Operations Manager
description:
Cin7 is a fast-growing global software company that provides solutions for modern-day product sellers. We help these sellers connect and simplify their operations, keep track of their inventory at scale, and help them sell their products across multiple sales channels around the world.

Cin7 is expanding very quickly with a mission to empower product sellers to thrive by making selling as easy as buying. We are committed to this mission to become the leading Inventory Management Software brand in the world.

Serving over 8,000 customers globally, processing more than 125 million orders per year, and supporting over $35B of Gross Merchandise Value, Cin7 has been rated best overall in inventory management software in 2024 by Forbes Advisor.

How you'll make an impact:
The Revenue Operations Manager owns the day-to-day running of our revenue operations cadences. This person keeps our go-to-market engine moving by supporting Acquisition, Payments, and Upsell motions, maintaining our sales tech stack, and delivering the recurring reports, data checks, and operational tasks that keep the team on track.
This is a hands-on role with a clear growth path. You will start by executing and owning core cadences, and over time grow into an operational partner for our front-line Sales Managers, helping them run their teams with better data, tighter processes, and faster answers.
This is an AI-native role. We expect you to use AI tools as a normal part of your daily work, and to keep finding ways to automate and improve how the team operates.


What you'll do:
Own Day-to-Day Cadences 
- 
 Run the weekly, monthly, and quarterly operational cadences for the Revenue Operations team, including pipeline reviews, forecast prep, and quarter-end close activities.
- 
 Complete the end-of-month commission audits (see below) on schedule.
- 
 Prepare and distribute recurring reports and dashboards on time and with accurate data.
- 
 Track open items and follow-ups from cadence meetings, and make sure they are closed.
 End-of-Month Commission Audits 
 Commission audits are a key monthly cadence for this role. Each month end, you will audit Internal Sales Commissions and Partner Commissions to confirm payouts are accurate, supported by the data, and compliant with the commission plans and approval rules.
- 
 Reconcile commission calculations against closed deals, bookings, and payments in Salesforce, and investigate and resolve any differences.
- 
 Check that deals, discounts, and partner attribution follow plan terms and DOAs before payouts are finalized.
- 
 Work with Sales leaders, Finance, and Partner teams to correct errors, handle exceptions, and document the outcome.
- 
 Keep a clear audit trail and an SOP for the process, and treat all commission and compensation data as confidential.
 Support Acquisition, Payments, and Upsell Motions 
- 
 Provide daily operational support to Sales and Account teams across new customer acquisition, payments, and upsell.
- 
 Process operational requests such as trial extensions, discount applications, account setups, and approvals in Salesforce, following Delegations of Authority (DOAs).
- 
 Keep accurate logs of discounts and approvals for audit compliance.
- 
 Monitor pipeline and opportunity health across each motion, and flag risks, gaps, and stalled deals to the team.
 Maintain the Sales Tech Stack

 Handle routine administration of Salesforce and connected tools (such as Gong, RevenueHero, Clay and Lean Data): users, permissions, picklists, fields, validation rules, and simple workflows.
- 
 Run scheduled data uploads and updates until automation is in place.
-

- 
 Triage and resolve user issues and system requests, and escalate larger changes to Ops leadership with context and a proposed solution.

Equinox seeks a dynamic and highly motivated Senior Manager to join our Treasury team. As Senior Manager, Treasury, you will lead corporate cash management, liquidity planning, and financial risk mitigation and hedging, while ensuring an optimal capital structure and regulatory compliance. 
 The ideal candidate will have excellent financial, analytical, leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills. The Treasury team works cross functionally to support all aspects of the organization - this individual should be a self-starter who is eager to roll up their sleeves, dive into details and drive decision making through financial analysis. This role reports to our Vice President of Finance and is based at our Park Avenue headquarters in New York City. If interested and qualified, please apply directly to the role online. 
 Responsibilities   
- Oversee daily cash operations including movement of cash between business units, wire transfers, optimization of debt costs and bank fees, and cash reporting. 
- Lead short-term and long-term cash forecasts. 
- Manage financial risk, including interest rate, foreign exchange, and commodity exposures, and lead hedging strategies to mitigate exposure. 
- Maintain relationships with banks and financial institutions; manage debt facilities and lender compliance requirements. 
- Provide valuable input on capital structure, investment strategies, and treasury transformation projects. 
- Manage the investment of excess cash and short-term investment portfolios, balancing yield, liquidity, and capital preservation. 
- Assist with financial due diligence for mergers, acquisitions, and capital fundraising. 
- Partner with FP&A and business leaders to support financial planning, budgeting, and strategic decision-making with treasury insights. 
- Lead system automation and efficiency in treasury tasks. 
- Ensure all treasury activities comply with internal policies and controls, and regulatory standards. 
- Mentor high-performing Treasury team, fostering a culture of analytics and collaboration.

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or Accounting is required. MBA or CTP preferred. 
- 8+ years of corporate treasury experience, preferably in a multinational organization, with 3+ years in a management role. 
- Investment banking experience is a plus. 
- Advanced proficiency in Excel and treasury management systems (TMS). 
- Proven leadership skills and ability to manage a small team. 
- Proven analytical, financial modeling and presentation skills with the ability to conduct detailed analyses, tell the story through data, and effectively summarize actionable recommendations. 
- Must be a proactive self-starter with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and responsibilities. 
- Results-oriented with strong attention to detail.  
- Excellent communication and collaboration skills. 
- Must be a team player who understands the importance of the role as a key support function to the organization
 Pay Transparency : $150k - $160k

AS A MEMBER OF THE EQUINOX TEAM YOU WILL RECEIVE:  
- We offer competitive salary, benefits, and industry leading commission opportunities for club employees 
- Complimentary Club membership 
- Perks and incentives with our products and services including Personal Training, Pilates, Spa and Shop 
 NOTE: This job description is intended to describe the general requirements for the position. It is not a complete statement of duties, responsibilities or requirements. Other duties not listed here may be assigned as necessary to ensure the proper operations of the department.  
 Equinox is an equal opportunity employer. For more information regarding our career opportunities, please visit one of our clubs or our website at  https://careers.equinox.com/  
 All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Must have a legal right to work in the United Kingdom.

title: Senior Manager, Subscription Analytics
description:
iFIT’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience. We develop proprietary software that learns and adjusts to the habits of each person as it delivers immersive content that guides them on their own individual fitness journey. 
 We are currently seeking an ambitious pace-setter to join our team as a Senior Manager, Subscription Analytics remotely in the US. 
 iFIT is a global fitness technology company that connects members to world-class trainers, immersive content, and smart equipment. The Senior Manager, Subscription Analytics is a key analytical partner within the Subscriptions organization, owning the metrics, models, and instrumentation that explain the health of iFIT’s subscription business and the in-app behavior that drives it. This role defines and governs the app event tracking strategy, builds funnel, engagement, and cohort analyses across the member journey, and connects product behavior to subscription, churn, and revenue outcomes. If you are a data-driven analytical leader who thrives on translating complex behavioral signals into strategic decisions, we want to hear from you. 
 ROLE COMMITMENTS 
- Own the measurement and forecast of app-only subscriber balance against annual subscriber and revenue targets, including funnel analytics from install and trial start through paid conversion and renewal. 
- Drive ARPU improvement by making monetization data self-serve across payment opportunities, refunds, onboarding flows, and saves. 
- Establish the engagement and retention foundation: cohort and lifecycle analyses, the leading indicators of retention and churn, and churn-propensity models. 
 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
- Own the app analytics framework, including event taxonomy, tracking plans, and instrumentation standards, partnering with Product and Engineering to ensure data is accurate, complete, and consistent across iOS, Android, web, and connected equipment. 
- Build and maintain funnel analytics from install and trial start through paid conversion, activation, and renewal, identifying drop-off points and sizing the opportunity. 
- Analyze user engagement and behavior including feature adoption, engagement frequency, and content consumption, and identify the leading indicators of retention and churn. 
- Develop cohort, retention, and lifecycle analyses, and translate behavioral signals into churn-risk and propensity models that CRM can act on. 
- Design and analyze A/B tests and experiments with Product and Growth teams, defining success metrics, sample sizing, and readouts. 
- Monitor subscription, churn, and revenue performance against forecast, and maintain forecasting and retention models. 
- Build and maintain dashboards and self-serve reporting that give Product, Finance, and CRM a shared view of subscriber health. 
 EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE 
 Education and Basic Qualifications 
- Hands-on experience with product analytics tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, or similar, and event-level data in a warehouse such as Snowflake. 
- Proficiency in SQL and Excel or spreadsheet-based financial modeling. 
- Experience with subscription, revenue, or churn analytics in a B2C or DTC environment. 
- Ability to translate data findings into forecasts and variance explanations for non-technical stakeholders. 
- Strong cross-functional communication and collaboration skills. 
- Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
- Experience with BI or reporting tools such as Tableau, Looker, or similar platforms. 
- Python or R proficiency for automation and advanced modeling. 
- Familiarity with billing or CRM systems. 
- Background in DTC subscription or e-commerce businesses. 
- Experience presenting data-driven analysis to senior leadership.

title: Manager, Corporate Finance
description:
WHO WE ARE

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, Booking.com http://Booking.com, H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank. 

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.



As Manager, Corporate Finance, you will own Imprint's financial planning and analysis function, with direct accountability for building the systems, models, and processes that power forward-looking financial decision-making.

This is a highly technical, hands-on role for someone who builds with code as naturally as they build with spreadsheets — and who is energized by replacing manual workflows with automated, scalable infrastructure. You will partner directly with the Deputy CFO and work cross-functionally with Commercial, Accounting, Treasury, Data and Engineering teams to bring rigor and speed to how Imprint forecasts, plans, and operates financially.

This role is right for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and has strong opinions about how modern finance teams should operate.

 - Built trusted working relationships with Commercial, Finance, Data, and Engineering teams

 - Demonstrated the ability to operate independently and iterate quickly on high-priority workstreams

Responsibilities

 - Own the design, build, and maintenance of Imprint's corporate financial model, transitioning it from Excel to Python-based infrastructure

 - Automate financial reporting and commentary workflows to reduce manual data pulling and accelerate insights delivery

 - Build and maintain forward-looking forecasts (3–6 month horizon) that give the business clear financial visibility

 - Partner with Commercial GMs and partner leads to incorporate revenue and cost inputs into planning models

 - Collaborate with Accounting on book close, cost pipeline, and reporting accuracy

 - Work with Treasury and Vendor Management on cash flow and cost forecasting

 - Support headcount planning and its impact on financial forecasts in partnership with the People team

 - Use AI tooling (e.g., Claude, Cursor) to build scalable, automated finance workflows

 - Identify and eliminate inefficiencies in how financial data is collected, modeled, and reported

 - Present financial insights clearly to senior stakeholders, translating complex outputs into actionable decisions

Qualifications

Required

 - Hands-on, working knowledge of Python — must have built models, scripts, or automated tools, not just theoretical familiarity
 - Demonstrated experience building with AI tools (e.g., Claude, Cursor, or similar) — this is a non-negotiable

About the Role
 The Sort Capacity Manager owns network-wide capacity de-risking for the Sort organization. This role builds and maintains the constraint model that defines what “de-risked capacity” means across every 1P and 3P facility — dock door availability, floor/pallet-position space, max throughput, and optimal labor and automation. 
 About the Team 
- Own the network constraint model — Model site capacity against its underlying constraints: dock door availability (inbound/outbound truck cadence by hour, translated from Mx forecast), floor/pallet-position space (inbound-to-outbound hourly volume vs. staging capacity), max throughput (automation vs. manual sortation rate, package profile mix, cross-dock vs. sort), and optimal labor hours required to hit max output.
- Govern spoke capacity data — Drive spoke capacity maintenance in the sort app, ensuring product reflects current facility configuration, and hold cross-functional partners accountable when it doesn't.
- Own zip-to-facility strategy — Own zip code-to-facility mapping and re-optimization as volume and rates shift, balancing service-level and cost trade-offs.
- Own device and consumable readiness — Forecast scanners, bins, and gaylords against site growth to avoid reactive procurement; own the readiness cadence end to end.
- Scope hub-to-spoke routing opportunities — Build the business case for hub-sort-to-spoke direct routing and bring recommendations forward to Network Design and Real Estate.
- Close forecasting product gaps — Identify where forecasting tools fail to capture capacity reality and drive the fix with Data/Product partners.
- Own Mx launch — Own Mx launch end to end, including CET allocation by merchant priority, negotiating trade-offs across competing merchant demands.
 You're excited about this opportunity because you will… 
- 3-6-12 month runway visibility ahead of any projected capacity constraint.
- Site launch recommendations delivered proactively, not reactively.
- % of high-priority Mx launches assigned an optimal CET.
 We're excited about you because you have…  
- Strategic model ownership — You've built and owned a capacity, forecasting, or network constraint model that became a standing input to planning — not a one-off analysis.
- Independent judgment — You can independently judge where the real bottleneck is across a large, multi-site network, without a pre-scoped problem statement.
- Cross-functional negotiation — You've negotiated trade-off recommendations with senior, cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., Network Design, Real Estate, Finance) and influenced capital-adjacent decisions.
- Physical operations fluency — You understand physical warehouse operations deeply enough to translate dock, floor, throughput, and labor constraints into a single model.
- Experience — 7+ years in supply chain, network strategy, or operations, with direct experience owning capacity planning or site launch strategy at scale.
- Executive communication — You communicate trade-offs and risk clearly and concisely to senior leadership, and you know what to escalate versus resolve independently.

title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.

 - AI across the Real Estate team: use Claude and custom agents to eliminate your own manual work, then go further. Identify where AI can save broader team time (market research, data pulls, memo drafting, lease and LOI summaries, pipeline reporting), build reusable prompts, skills, and agents, train teammates to use them, and track the time saved. Be honest about where AI output needs human review.
 - Market packs and benchmarks: produce market entry recommendations, ranked pipeline views, and site-level briefs, backed by per-site cost and occupancy benchmarks by market so deal comparison sits on real data.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.
 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.
 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.
 - Comfort with census, consumer spend, mobility, and first-party data, and honesty about the limits of each.
 - Financial literacy: you can build a basic site pro forma, calculate payback and break-even, and connect a demand forecast to a real estate decision.
 - Flexibility. You can tear down your own model without ego, rebuild it when the facts change, and stay organized while priorities shift.
 - Clear communication and intellectual honesty. You can defend an assumption to a skeptical executive in two minutes, name the two things most likely to be wrong, and say early when the data does not support the answer people want.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
 - SQL or Python, which helps you work alongside engineers.
 - Specific, demonstrable use of AI to speed up analytical work, and real interest in teaching others to do the same.
 - Exposure to healthcare or regulated markets, or to European or multi-region expansion.

AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of building financial models, analyzing business performance, and generating investment research. Yet complex financial decisions still demand the experience, critical thinking, and professional judgment of seasoned finance experts.

 - Proficiency in Excel financial modeling and tools such as Capital IQ, Bloomberg, FactSet, PitchBook, or financial planning software.

 - Interest in artificial intelligence, large language models (LLMs), and AI applications in financial services.

Leap is one of the fastest-growing benefits solutions and a category-defining pioneer in employer specialty pharmacy. We are reshaping how life-changing therapies are delivered and financed, ensuring patients get the treatment they need while employers finally get a fair deal.

You’ll also become an expert in our Impact Analysis framework, helping our most strategic buyers understand the value of Leap and keeping the partner story and the employer savings story tied to the same numbers.This role reports into the Director of Business Operation and works closely with the Networks, Manufacturer, Growth, Engineering and Data teams.

NETWORK, DEMAND, AND PARTNER ANALYTICS

 - Score bids and rate cards from specialty pharmacies, manufacturers, infusion providers and nursing agencies against Leap’s price targets, and turn the results into feedback Networks uses in negotiations

 - Build prevalence and volume models from claims and membership data to project demand by drug, therapeutic area and region

 - Build geographic capacity models that show where infusion center and nursing coverage falls short of projected membership, and where to expand next

 - Build the case for drug manufacturers: the members, volume and sites of care Leap brings them


TURN ANALYSES INTO TOOLS

 - Define requirements for our 2027 buy-side tools (rate-card comparison, preferred-partner routing, price tracking, A–F pricing grades) and partner with Engineering to ship them

 - Run those tools day to day and keep improving their accuracy and speed

 - Replace recurring manual analysis with AI-enabled workflows that other teams can run without you


CLIENT-FACING CLAIMS ANALYSIS & SALES ENABLEMENT

 - Partner with the enterprise sales team on strategic deals, tailoring analyses for prospects, brokers and benefits consultants

 - Run Leap’s Impact Analysis tooling and apply your understanding of healthcare claims data to build analyses for benefits leaders at some of the largest US employers, written for a CFO or benefits committee

 - Build templates, frameworks and tools that let the sales team deliver strong proposals at scale, so every prospect gets our best analysis

 - Find patterns across our book: which drugs and categories drive consistent savings, and what that means for how we price and target


CONNECT THE BUY AND SELL SIDE OF OUR BUSINESS

 - Explore pricing model tradeoffs between client savings and movements in network pricing

 - Help prioritize drug and network efforts that accelerate growth across client segments

 - Deliver CEO-level recommendations on investment and partnership decisions




QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - 4-8+ years of experience in analytics, strategy or a similarly quantitative role

 - Track record of building rigorous analyses and models from scratch, including in Excel

 - Hands-on experience using AI and agentic tools to build and scale analyses

 - Ability to take messy data, find the insight and communicate it as a clear recommendation

 - Confidence presenting recommendations to executive audiences (internal and external)

 - Experience building scalable tools or processes in partnership with product or engineering teams


PREFERRED

 - Background in Management consulting (ideally life sciences) or investment banking, or analytics and strategy at a drug manufacturer, PBM, specialty pharmacy or health tech company

 - Experience in healthcare delivery, specialty pharmacy or drug pricing

 - Hands-on experience with healthcare claims data

title: Enterprise Strategy Associate
description:
ABOUT US:

Camber builds software to improve the quality and accessibility of healthcare. We streamline and replace manual work so clinicians can focus on what they do best: providing great care. For more details on our thesis, check out our write-up: What is Camber? https://camberhealth.notion.site/What-is-Camber-1a6c4e2fa5318049b6beef91b8ed7d1a?pvs=4

We’ve raised $50M in funding from phenomenal supporters at a16z, Craft Ventures, YCombinator, Manresa, and many others who are committed to improving the accessibility of care. For more information, take a look at: Announcing Camber https://www.camber.health/knowledge/launch


ABOUT OUR CULTURE:

Our mission to change behavioral health starts with us and how we operate. We don’t want to just change behavioral health, we want to change the way startups operate. Here are a few tactical examples:

1) Improving accessibility and quality of healthcare is something we live and breathe. Everyone on Camber’s team cares deeply about helping clinicians and patients.

2) We have to have a sense of humor. Healthcare is so broken, it's depressing if you don't laugh with us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Camber is hiring an Enterprise Strategy Associate to partner with our Director of Enterprise Revenue to build the narrative behind our largest client partnerships. Revenue cycle is the bloodline of a clinic, and through data, you build trust with the client. You will drive the narrative that helps a clinic understand the impact Camber can have on its business, and you’ll use it to shape the strategy of the deal.

This is not a traditional analyst role. You will follow a clinic through its entire time at Camber, from the first conversation to a fully rolled-out partnership, and keep driving the value of Camber at every step. You will join a team that values agency, intellectual honesty, and a “rowing in the same direction” mentality.

Your time will be split across three stages of the client journey:

 - Go-to-Market: You leverage a clinic’s data to build the narrative for how Camber can impact its revenue cycle, partnering with a Director of Enterprise Revenue on the analysis and story to win the deal.

 - Implementation: You are the subject-matter expert on both Camber and the clinic, and that expertise drives how we serve them. You help make sure the value of Camber is seen and understood as we roll out.

 - Stable State: You work with the strategic account management team to inform and prepare material for the clinic’s key decision-makers to help them understand the impact Camber is having on their business.


WHAT YOU’LL DO


BE THE ANALYTICAL AND NARRATIVE BACKBONE OF THE DEAL

 - Run Diagnostics: Dig into a clinic’s billing, claims, and payment data to find where revenue is being left on the table (e.g., denial trends, underpayments, aging AR, payer-specific patterns).

 - Build the Business Case: Size the opportunity in dollars and collection rate points, and build the ROI models that decision-makers use to say yes.

 - Drive the Strategy of the Deal: Use what the data says to decide where the deal goes: which problems to lead with, what each stakeholder cares about, and what a pilot needs to prove.

 - Build Executive-Ready Materials: Turn analysis into crisp, top-down stories that client leaders can act on and take to their own leadership.


IDENTIFY WHAT REALLY MATTERS

 - Ready the Internal Team: Surface what a new enterprise account or vertical will demand (e.g., net-new integrations, custom analyses, reporting needs) and get Product, Engineering, Data, and Operations ahead of it before go-live.

 - Flag Early: Act as the account’s early-warning system. When something in the data or the relationship looks off, raise it to the right people before it becomes a fire.


ANCHOR THE CLIENT ON CAMBER’S IMPACT

 - Own the Data Relationship: Be the go-to partner for the client’s data and analytics leads through the pilot and beyond.

 - Prove and Communicate Value: Track performance against the baseline and tell the story of Camber’s impact in recurring business reviews. Delivering results is half the job. Making sure the client knows about them is the other half.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience: 1–3 years in management consulting, investment banking, or strategy at a fast-moving startup.

 - Data Fluency: Experience working with large, messy data sets and turning them into conclusions that drive decisions.

 - Customer and Executive Exposure: Previous experience working directly with customers and senior executives.

 - Commercial Instinct: You understand how businesses make money and what motivates the people making the decision, and you can tie your analysis back to both.

 - Learning Velocity: Healthcare or RCM experience is a plus but not required. What matters more is that you do your homework, ask sharp questions, and ramp quickly into a complex domain.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - The ability to turn analysis into a narrative that moves a decision, not just a data dump.

 - “Client hands”: you’re comfortable and credible in front of a client, and you can hold your ground when the room pushes back.

 - A high bar for detail. Every number you put in front of a client is one you can defend.

 - High agency: you take ownership of ambiguous problems and create structure where none exists.

 - A collaborative spirit. You know when to pull in other teams, and you aren’t shy about asking for what you need.

 - Humility: you seeak out critique and get better because of it.


PERKS & BENEFITS AT CAMBER:

 - Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans with nationwide coverage, including 24/7 virtual urgent care.

 - Mental Health Support: Weekly therapy reimbursement up to $100, so you can prioritize the care that works best for you.

 - Paid Parental Leave: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid time off for new parents (birth, adoption, or foster care).

 - Financial Wellness: 401K (traditional & Roth), HSA & FSA options, and monthly commuter benefits

REVENUE OPERATIONS LEAD

Location: USA Remote / San Francisco, CA · Full-Time

 


ABOUT ANDROMEDA

Andromeda is a market and infrastructure platform to buy, sell, and operate compute.

We believe demand for compute will grow exponentially. So fast that a handful of vertically integrated providers won't be able to scale across operations, capital, supply chains, and politics to serve it. The result is a massive wave of fragmentation, with AI factories of every shape and size coming to market to fill this demand. Our job is to enable all of that fragmented compute to flow through one platform, delivering reliable capacity to model builders, research labs, and inference providers when they need it. We believe every spare electron should be made productive for AI and we're building the platform that makes that possible.


We sit at the center of three forces:

 - Companies that need reliable, high-performance compute fast

 - A fragmented global supply of GPUs across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and independent data centers

 - Capital, risk, and operational complexity that most teams are not equipped to manage

When we succeed, trillions of dollars of compute will flow through Andromeda. Builders get capacity when they need it. Providers get a reliable way to monetize, operate, and finance infrastructure at scale. Capital gets an easy way to deploy, hedge, and underwrite.

In five years, Andromeda won't just participate in the AI infrastructure market. We will shape it.

 


THE ROLE

This is a chance to join Andromeda as our first Revenue Operations Lead — a strategic partner to Sales, Customer Success, and leadership as we scale a GPU compute market moving through its first real step-change in revenue. You'll own the operating system behind the number: pipeline hygiene, forecasting, deal desk process, supply administration, and the connective tissue between sales, supply, legal, and finance.

 

There's no playbook to inherit here. Our systems don't yet talk to each other the way they should, our routing and RACI are still being formalized, and the revenue org is being built from scratch. If you're an analytical operator who thrives in unstructured environments and loves bringing order to chaos, this role gives you the room to build it — and a path to leading revenue operations as the team grows.

 

What You’ll Do 

● GTM tech stack: Own and optimize HubSpot (current CRM) — field standardization, data hygiene cadence, and integrations so deal blockers, supply status, and pipeline data actually stay in sync.

● Forecasting & reporting infrastructure: Build and maintain the dashboards and forecast rollups sales leadership relies on for weekly deal reviews — pipeline health, coverage, and revenue performance against target.

● Deal desk & process design: Run the routing logic between strategic and velocity deals, own the RACI as the org scales, and close the sequencing gaps between customer and provider contracting.

● Planning & compensation: Partner with sales leadership and finance on capacity planning, quota design, and comp modeling

● AI-driven efficiency: Identify where AI tools and workflows can cut manual work out of reporting, forecasting, and deal ops — you'll be operating inside a team that already runs a lot of its own workflow through AI, and should be looking to extend that.

● Cross-functional glue: Sit at the intersection of sales, supply/ops, legal, and finance. Identify friction points in our business and get us unblocked.

 

What We’re Looking For

● Experience: 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Business Operations at a high-growth B2B company — ideally one with usage-based, capacity-based, or infrastructure pricing (compute, cloud, hosting).

● CRM fluency: Hands-on CRM ownership at scale — you've built field architecture, workflows, and hygiene process, not just pulled reports.

● Systems thinking with a long-term view: You design for what a process looks like six months after go-live, not just whether it works on day one.
● Builder, not maintainer: You've owned a process end to end — comp calculations, forecasting model, deal desk — not just supported someone else running it. Comfortable standing up infrastructure from scratch.
● High agency, high ambiguity tolerance: This role sits across sales, supply, legal, and finance, and the "way it's supposed to work" is still being defined in real time.
● Directness: Shows up with proposals instead of open questions, and is comfortable being the source of truth on numbers people won't always like — forecast misses, comp disputes.

At Armadin, we're a group of engineers, researchers, and security researchers on a mission to redefine what proactive security can do in the AI era. Cyberattacks are becoming autonomous and relentless and we believe defending against threats before they materialize is one of the most powerful ways to protect the institutions the world depends on.



We're building autonomous proactive security from the ground up, reinforcing the tradecraft of elite security practioners into purpose-built security models and agents that discover risk and remediate it before organizations are breached.



Led by Kevin Mandia, founder of Mandiant ($5.4B exit to Google), our team brings together researchers and engineers from Google, xAI, Meta, Stanford, Georgia Tech, Waterloo, Berkeley, and MIT to reinvent security for an adversary that never sleeps.



Role Overview

As a Senior FP&A Analyst for Services, you'll own the financial engine behind our services delivery: the people, partners, and hours that turn adversarial expertise into customer outcomes. You'll build services cost and margin models from scratch, turn messy operational data into decisions, and use AI to move faster than any traditional finance team.

You'll partner directly with Expertise (Services) and Delivery leadership to understand how work is scoped, staffed, and delivered, then show them exactly what it costs and where margin is won or lost. You'll own the monthly services cost close, build forecasts that inform hiring and pricing decisions, and operate with radical autonomy and speed.

What You'll Do

Own Services COGS & Margin

 - Own the monthly services COGS close, including variance analysis across labor, subcontractors, travel, and tooling. Explain what moved and why, not just what the numbers are.

 - Build and maintain engagement-level and practice-level margin models covering assessments, red team engagements, incident response, and retainers.

 - Track utilization, realization, billable vs. non-billable time, and bench costs to surface where capacity is being lost.

Shape Pricing, Scoping & Capacity Decisions

 - Build the services cost model that informs rate cards, fixed-fee vs. T&M structures, retainer economics, and deal scoping.

 - Partner with Services leadership on capacity planning, forecasting headcount and subcontractor needs against pipeline and backlog.

 - Model the economics of new offerings, delivery models, and staffing mixes before they launch.

Be the Data Wizard

 - Pull, join, and clean data across time tracking, PSA, CRM, HRIS, and ERP systems to build a single source of truth for services performance.

 - Write SQL and scripts to build models, dashboards, and KPIs that leaders actually use.

 - Find the signal in messy operational data: overruns, scope creep, underpriced work, and staffing inefficiencies.

Make AI a Core Part of the Finance Workflow

 - Use AI and LLM tools daily to accelerate analysis, automate cost pulls and variance commentary, and generate reporting.

 - Build AI-assisted workflows that let the team close faster and forecast with more confidence.

 - Evaluate and implement tools that raise the bar on planning, forecasting, and reporting.

Drive FP&A Planning & Partner with Leadership

 - Own the services portions of the monthly close, quarterly forecast, and annual budget; build rolling forecasts for hiring, pricing, and resourcing.

 - Present services performance and margin reviews to leadership and the board.

 - Act as a true business partner on headcount, pricing, go-to-market strategy, and delivery scaling.

What You'll Bring

 - 5–7 years in FP&A or finance with direct ownership of professional services, consulting, or managed services costs, ideally inside a cybersecurity or technology company with a significant services arm.

 - Deep fluency in services economics: utilization, realization, blended rates, bill rates vs. cost rates, subcontractor management, and engagement-level P&L.

 - Data wizard skills: advanced SQL, advanced Excel or Sheets, and scripting (Python or similar). You can pull your own data, build your own models, and automate your own reporting.

 - Strong, hands-on AI skills. You already use LLM tools to work faster and can show how they've changed the way you analyze and report.

 - Startup operator mentality: self-directed, comfortable with ambiguity, and owns outcomes independently.

 - Clear communicator who can explain margin and cost drivers to practitioners, delivery leaders, and executives.

Even Better With

 - Experience in the services finance org of a security leader such as an incident response, red team, or security consulting practice.

 - Built a services margin or capacity model from scratch, or stood up services FP&A at a high-growth company.

 - Experience with Harvest or similar time-tracking and PSA tools.

 - Exposure to cloud, compute, or AI cost modeling.

 - History of working in high-autonomy, high-stakes environments.

ABOUT CLIPBOARD

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

 


ROLE OVERVIEW

The Strategic WFM Analyst lives in the Core Workforce Management (WFM) Planning & Operations Strategy team and is responsible for owning centralized forecast, capacity planning, workforce cost optimization, and strategic headcount trade-offs across all lines of business (LOBs). Moving beyond traditional scheduling and intraday monitoring, this role acts as a high-judgment governance function, translating complex demand forecasts into defensible FTE, BPO, and overtime spend strategies, modelling capacity risks, and aligning executive stakeholders across Finance, Product, and Operations. You are exceptionally strong in WFM maths and financial analytics, exhibit deep strategic curiosity, navigate messy raw data effortlessly, and communicate recommendations with executive-level clarity.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Translating multi-LOB demand forecasts into monthly and quarterly capacity, headcount, and budget requirements.

 - Modelling workforce and financial trade-offs across internal FTEs, BPO partners, overtime spend, bonus hours, productivity shifts, and shrinkage.

 - Analyzing demand-funnel changes (e.g., product feature roll outs, AI bot deflection shifts) and quantifying their exact capacity and dollar blast radius.

 - Partnering directly with Finance, Product, and Operations to validate baseline assumptions, enforce input SLAs, and align on staffing commitments.

 - Drafting concise, decision-ready executive memos and Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs) for Directors and leadership.

 - Conducting deep-dive root-cause analyses whenever operational actuals deviate from capacity plans and establishing corrective action paths.

 - Standardizing capacity planning frameworks, modeling templates, and operating standards across LOBs.

 - Maintaining deep forecasting competency to audit models, challenge underlying assumptions, and provide seamless coverage across the broader central WFM engine.

 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strategic WFM Maths: Exceptionally strong quantitative background with deep expertise in WFM fundamentals (capacity modelling, Erlang, shrinkage, AHT, SLA/ASA trade-offs) and advanced proficiency in Google Sheets, SQL, or Python.

 - Business & Financial Judgement: Demonstrated ability to connect operational queue dynamics directly to dollar exposure, hiring velocity, BPO costs, and SLA risk.

 - Executive Communication: Superior strategic writing skills with a natural instinct to distil complex, multi-variable workforce analytics into scannable, 1-2 page decision memos.

 - Cross-Functional Influence: Proven ability to establish governance frameworks, challenge bad assumptions with back tested data, and align Finance, Product, and Operations leadership without formal authority.

 - Blank-Page Ownership: High comfort operating in ambiguous environments with incomplete data, verifiably isolating what materially matters without requiring step-by-step direction.

 - WFM Analyst Profile: Strong core WFM domain expertise with a strategic/Ops spike, not a generalist and not a passive traditional scheduler.

 
 


HIRING PROCESS

 3. Case Study Interview - Technical & Capacity Interview

 4. Executive Judgement & Strategic Interview

 5. Culture Interview (People Ops)

 6. Offer

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

TRM is hiring a Strategic Finance Lead, R&D and AI to help decide how the company invests in AI, cloud and compute infrastructure, and the engineering capacity behind its products. You'll be the dedicated finance partner to the CTO and R&D leadership, turning complex usage, billing, and headcount data into recommendations that shape major investment decisions before they're made. Reporting to Pharoah Green, Head of Strategic Finance and FP&A, within the FP&A and Strategic Finance Business Partnership function, you'll design the financial architecture for R&D from the ground up, with AI built into how the work gets done.


The impact you will have:

 - Shape how TRM invests in AI, cloud, and compute by building an AI-assisted, driver-based economic model that connects usage and billing data across hundreds of SKUs to forecasts and decisions.

 - Lower R&D costs as a % of revenue without slowing product velocity, using AI to surface optimization opportunities in infrastructure spend and partnering with Engineering to act on them.

 - Define TRM's AI spend strategy with the Head of AI, using AI-powered analysis to track spend against ROI by tool and workload and to recommend where to commit, consolidate, or build.

 - Give R&D leaders an early view of change by owning planning, forecasting, and the headcount capacity model, with automated workflows that flag risks while there is still time to act.

 - Influence major infrastructure and R&D commitments by leading investment cases from business case to decision to measurement, with AI-assisted scenario analysis that makes tradeoffs clear.

 - Turn R&D performance into a clear executive and board narrative: what changed, why, and which decisions should follow.

 - Rebuild R&D finance around AI, automation, and Pigment so more time goes to shaping decisions and less to assembling reports.

What we're looking for:

 - 7+ years across strategic finance, FP&A, business operations, or a related role. We care more about the complexity you've owned and the influence you've had than an exact number of years.

 - A record of owning consequential work end to end: framing an ambiguous question, structuring the analysis, forming a point of view, and driving a recommendation to action.

 - Strong data-informed modeling skills, including driver-based forecasts, investment cases, and capacity models built from incomplete or complex data, accelerated with AI.

 - Hands-on experience analyzing cloud, compute, AI, or other usage-based technology costs, and experience partnering with Engineering, Product, Data, AI, or Infrastructure leaders.

 - The judgment and communication skills to become a trusted partner to senior technical leaders, challenge assumptions constructively, and explain financial implications in plain language.

 - Applied AI fluency: you can show how you've used AI to improve the speed or quality of modeling, research, or recurring workflows, and how you check the reliability of its output.

 - Curiosity to learn technical systems quickly and translate how AI products and modern infrastructure scale into financial insight.

About the Team:

 - Strategic Finance is a small, high-leverage team that works directly with TRM's leadership on planning, investment decisions, and company-wide strategy.

 - Our job isn't just to explain the numbers. We collaborate with leaders to make better decisions, and we hold a high bar for rigor and trust in our work.

 - You'll have substantial ownership from day one, direct exposure to the CTO and executive team, and room to shape how R&D finance operates.

 - The role is built to scale with its owner. Using AI and automation, you can expand what one person owns, and as the mandate grows there may be an opportunity to build a team.
Team Operating Rhythms:
 - We're distributed, not distant: written communication for clarity and context, live time for decisions and collaboration.
 - Regular working sessions with the CTO and R&D leaders, plus a monthly R&D cost and forecast review.
